If it is said: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever does that, then he has nothing with God﴾, and this is the description of a disbeliever.

We say: the meaning of the verse is "then he has nothing of the guardianship (wilāyah) of God," and this does not necessitate disbelief in prohibiting the allegiance to disbelievers.

Know that He, exalted is He, sent down many verses with this meaning, among them His saying: ﴿Do not take intimates from other than yourselves﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 118], and His saying: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 22], and His saying: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 51], and His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtaḥanah: 1], and He said: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71].

Know that the believer's being an ally of a disbeliever admits three aspects:

One: that he be content with his disbelief and support him because of it. This is forbidden, because everyone who does that is approving of that religion, and approving of disbelief is disbelief, and contentment with disbelief is disbelief, so it is impossible for him to remain a believer while having this attribute.

If it is said: Did He not say: ﴿And whoever does that, then he has nothing with God﴾, and this does not necessitate disbelief, so he is not included under this verse, since He said: ﴿O you who believe﴾ [al-Mumtaḥanah: 1]? Then the address must be concerning something with which the believer remains a believer.

Second: good companionship in the world outwardly, and this is not forbidden.

The third division, which is intermediate between the first two, is that allegiance to disbelievers in the sense of inclining toward them, assisting them, backing them, and supporting them, whether because of kinship or because of affection while believing that their religion is false. This does not necessitate disbelief, but it is forbidden, because allegiance in this sense may lead him to approve of their way and be content with their religion, and that takes him out of Islam. Therefore God, exalted is He, threatened concerning it, saying: ﴿And whoever does that, then he has nothing with God﴾.

If it is said: why could the intended meaning of the verse not be the prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies in the sense of allying with them instead of the believers? As for when they ally with them and ally with the believers together with them, that is not forbidden. Also, His saying: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies﴾ contains an added nuance, because a man may be an ally of another without taking him as an ally; so the prohibition of taking him as an ally does not necessitate the prohibition of allegiance itself.

We say: these two possibilities, although they may apply to the verse, are refuted by the other verses which indicate that their allegiance is not permissible.

The second issue: the dhāl of (yattakhidh) is kasrah because it is jussive by the prohibition, and it was vowelized because of the meeting of two sukūns. Al-Zajjāj said: "If it were read with a raf' as a statement, it would be permissible, and the meaning under the raf' would be that whoever is a believer should not take a disbeliever as an ally."

Know that the meaning of the prohibition and the meaning of the statement are close, because whenever the attribute of the believer is that he does not ally with the disbeliever, he is necessarily prohibited from allying with the disbeliever, and whenever he is prohibited from that, it is necessarily part of his character and way that he does not do that.

The third issue: His saying: ﴿instead of the believers﴾ means "other than the believers," like His saying: ﴿and call your witnesses besides God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23], i.e., other than God. That is because the word dūn is specific to place. You say: Zayd sat dūn ʿAmr, i.e., in a place lower than him. Then whoever is separate from another in place is different from him, so the word dūn was used in the sense of ghayr (other than). Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever does that, then he has nothing with God﴾, and there is an ellipsis in it; the meaning is "then he has nothing of the guardianship of God whereby the name of guardianship applies to him," meaning that he has completely withdrawn from the guardianship of God, exalted is He. This is an intelligible matter, for allegiance to an ally and allegiance to his enemy are opposites. The poet said:

You love my enemy, then you claim that you are my friend; the folly is not far from you.

It is also possible that the meaning is: "then he has nothing of the religion of God," and this is more eloquent.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿except that you fear from them a fear﴾, and in it there are issues:

The first issue: al-Kisā'ī read tuqāh with imālah; Nāfi' and Ḥamzah read it between tafkhīm and imālah; the rest read it with tafkhīm. Ya'qūb read taqiyyah. Imālah was permitted to indicate that the alif is from a yā', and tuqāh is of the measure fu'lah, like tu'dah and tukhmah. As for the one who reads with tafkhīm, it is because of the heavy letter, which is the qāf.

The second issue: al-Wāḥidī said: "taqaytuhu tuqāh, tuqan, tuqyah, taqwā." When you say ittaqaytu, its verbal noun is al-ittiqā'. He said "tattaqū" and then said "tuqāh" and did not say "ittiqā'," since it is a noun placed in the position of the verbal noun, as one says: jalasa jalsah and rakiba rakbah. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So his Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow a good growth﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 37]. The poet said:

And after your giving, the hundred camels grazing (al-ri'āʿ).

He treated it as the way of the giving (iʿṭā'). He said: it is also permissible to make tuqāh here like rummāh, so that it is an emphatic circumstantial accusative (ḥāl mu'akkidah).

The third issue: "al-Ḥasan said: Musaylimah the liar took two men from the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said to one of them: 'Do you testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God?' He said: 'Yes, yes, yes.' He said: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of God?' He said: 'Yes.' Musaylimah used to claim that he was the messenger of the Banū Ḥanīfah and Muḥammad was the messenger of Quraysh. So he left him and called the other and said: 'Do you testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of God?' He said: 'I am deaf,' three times. So he sent him forward and killed him. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: 'As for this one who was killed, he went on in his certainty and truthfulness, so congratulations to him. As for the other, he accepted the concession of God, so there is no blame upon him.'"

Know that the parallel to this verse is His saying: ﴿except one who is compelled while his heart is at rest with faith﴾ [al-Naḥl: 106].

* * *

The fourth issue: know that taqiyyah has many rulings, and we mention some of them.

The first ruling: taqiyyah is only when a man is among disbelieving people and fears for his self and property, so he conciliates them with the tongue. That is by not openly showing enmity with the tongue. Rather, it is also permissible to utter speech that suggests affection and allegiance, but on condition that he conceals the opposite and makes allusions in everything he says, for taqiyyah's effect is in the outward, not in the states of the hearts.

The second ruling of taqiyyah: if he declares faith and truth openly where taqiyyah is permitted for him, that would be more excellent, and its proof is what we mentioned in the story of Musaylimah.

The third ruling of taqiyyah: it is permitted only in what relates to displaying allegiance and enmity, and it may also be permitted in what relates to displaying the religion. As for what returns harm to others, such as killing, adultery, seizing property, false testimony, slandering chaste women, and revealing the weaknesses of the Muslims to the disbelievers, that is absolutely not permitted.

The fourth ruling: the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that taqiyyah is only permitted with dominant disbelievers. However, the school of al-Shāfi'ī, may God be pleased with him, holds that if the situation among Muslims resembles the situation between Muslims and polytheists, taqiyyah becomes permitted as protection of the self.

The fifth ruling: taqiyyah is permitted for the preservation of the self. As for whether it is permitted for the preservation of property, it is possible to rule that it is permitted, based on His (ﷺ) saying: "The sanctity of a Muslim's property is like the sanctity of his blood," and His (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr," and because the need for property is severe; if water is sold at a loss, the obligation of wuḍū' falls and it is permissible to limit oneself to tayammum to avert that amount of loss of property. So how would it not be permitted here? And God knows best.

The sixth ruling: Mujāhid said: this ruling was established at the beginning of Islam because of the weakness of the believers; but after the strength of the state of Islam, it no longer applies. 'Awf narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: "Taqiyyah is permitted for the believers until the Day of Resurrection." This view is more preferable, because averting harm from the self is obligatory to the extent possible.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God warns you of Himself﴾, and in it there are two views:

The first: that there is an omitted element, and the estimation is: "God warns you of the punishment of Himself." Abū Muslim said: the meaning of ﴿God warns you of Himself﴾ is: that you disobey Him and thereby deserve His punishment. The benefit in mentioning "Himself" is that if He had said "God warns you," this would not indicate that what is intended to be warned against is a punishment issuing from God or from another. When He mentioned "Himself," this confusion was removed. It is known that the punishment issuing from Him is the greatest kind of punishment, since He is capable of what has no limit, and no one has the power to repel Him or prevent Him from what He wills.

The second view: that the "self" here refers to taking disbelievers as allies, i.e., God forbids them from the very act itself.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And to God is the final return﴾, and the meaning is: God warns you of His punishment at your return to God.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, forbade the believers from taking the disbelievers as allies outwardly and inwardly, and made an exception to that in outward appearance for taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation), He followed this with a warning, so that the inner state would conform to the outer in the time of taqiyya. This is because whoever proceeds, during taqiyya, to display allegiance, his proceeding to that action outwardly may become a cause for that allegiance to arise inwardly. Therefore, He, exalted is He, made clear that He knows the inner states just as He knows the outer ones, so that the servant knows that He will surely requite him for everything he resolves upon in his heart. There are questions concerning the verse:

The first question: This verse is a conditional sentence. His saying ﴿Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it﴾ is the condition, and His saying ﴿Allah knows it﴾ is the consequence. Without doubt, the consequence is contingent upon the condition and comes after it. This seems to imply that the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is newly come into being.

The answer: The relation of Allah's knowledge to the fact that something has now occurred does not come about except when it occurs now. Then, this change and renewal has taken place only in the relations, the attributions and the connections, not in the reality of the knowledge itself. This question has a profound depth and it is mentioned in the science of kalam (theology).

The second question: The seat of intentions and inward thoughts is the heart, so why did He say ﴿what is in your breasts﴾ and not say "what is in your hearts"?

The answer: Because the heart is in the breast, it is permissible to put the breast in the place of the heart, as He said: ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾ [An-Nas: 5] and He said: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj: 46].

Page 14
The third question: If this verse is a warning concerning everything that occurs to the mind, then it is the imposition of what cannot be borne.

The answer: We have mentioned the detailed discussion of this matter at the end of Surat al-Baqarah, in His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 284].

* * *
Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah﴾.
Know that it is in the nominative case as a resumptive (new) sentence, like His saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [At-Tawbah: 14], where the verbs are in the jussive, then He said: ﴿and Allah relents﴾ [At-Tawbah: 15], where it is in the nominative. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So if Allah should will, He would seal over your heart and Allah would erase falsehood﴾ [Ash-Shura: 24], in the nominative. And in His saying ﴿And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾ there is the utmost warning, for if nothing in them is hidden from Him, how could the inner thought be hidden from Him?

* * *
Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, as a completion of the warning. This is because, when He made clear that He, exalted is He, knows all that is known, He knows what is in the heart, and He knows the measures of what is deserved of reward and punishment. Then He made clear that He is capable of all that is capable of being done, so He is necessarily capable of delivering each person's right to him. Thus in this is the completion of promise and threat, and of encouragement and warning.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 30:

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that were a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself. And Allah is Most Kind to His servants.﴾

Know that this verse belongs to the category of encouragement (al-targhib) and warning (al-tarhib), and it completes the discourse that preceded it.

Within it are several issues:

**The first issue:** They have mentioned several views concerning what governs the word "the Day" (yawma) in His statement "on the Day":

The first: Ibn al-Anbari said: "the Day" is connected to "the final return" (al-masir), and the implied meaning is: "And to Allah is the final return on the Day when you find."

The second: What governs it is His statement ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ in the preceding verse, as if He said: "And Allah warns you of Himself on that Day."

The third: What governs it is His statement ﴿And Allah is Powerful over all things﴾, meaning: He is Powerful on that Day when every soul finds what it has done of good present. This Day was singled out for mention, although other days are equal to it in relation to the power of Allah the Exalted, as a way of giving it preference because of its great importance, like His statement ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Fatiha: 4].

The fourth: What governs it is His statement "it wishes" (tawaddu), and the meaning is: every soul wishes such-and-such on that Day.

The fifth: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative by an implied verb, and the implied meaning is: "And remember the Day when every soul finds."

**The second issue:** Know that deeds do not remain, and it is not possible to find them on the Day of Resurrection, so an interpretation (ta'wil) is necessary here, and it is of two kinds:

The first: that one finds the scrolls of deeds. This is His statement the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We used to have it copied down what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29], and He said: ﴿Allah has enumerated it while they forgot it﴾ [al-Mujadila: 6].

The second: that one finds the recompense of deeds. His statement the Exalted, "present" (muhdaran), may mean that those scrolls will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection. It may also mean that the recompense of the deed will be brought forth, like His statement: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. On both interpretations, both encouragement and warning are achieved.

* * *

As for His statement ﴿and what it has done of evil, it wishes that between itself and that were a great distance﴾, there are two issues concerning it:

**The first issue:** Al-Wahidi said: The most apparent view is to make "ma" here equivalent to "alladhi" (who/that), with "'amilat" being its relative clause (sila), and it being conjoined to the first "ma". It is not permissible for "ma" to be conditional (shartiyya, i.e., "whatever"), because otherwise "tawaddu" would have to be in the accusative or genitive, and no one read it except with the nominative. This is evidence that "ma" here means "alladhi."

If it is said: Is it valid for it to be conditional according to the reading of Abdullah, "waddat"?

We say: There is no dispute about its validity, but treating it as a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar) is more fitting, because it is a description of the condition of the disbeliever on that Day, and it agrees more with the well-known reading.

**The second issue:** The "waw" in His statement ﴿and what it has done of evil﴾ has two views:

The first, which is the view of Abu Muslim al-Isfahani: the "waw" is the conjunctive waw ('atf), and the implied meaning is: "it finds what it has done of good and what it has done of evil." As for His statement ﴿it wishes that between itself and that were a great distance﴾, there are two possibilities concerning it: The first: it is a description (sifa) of "evil," and the implied meaning is: "and what it has done of evil, which it wishes would be far between it and itself." The second: that it is a circumstantial clause (hal), and the implied meaning is: "On the Day when it finds what it has done of evil present, in the state in which it wishes for its distance from it."

The second view: the "waw" is for resumption (li'l-isti'naf), and on this view the verse is not evidence for the certainty of the punishment of the wrongdoers. This is the place of generosity and kindness. This is because, regarding the reward, He explicitly stated that it is "present," but regarding the punishment, He did not state presence. Rather, He mentioned that they wish to flee from it and to be distant from it. This alerts that the side of promise is more likely to be realized than the side of threat.

**The third issue:** "al-amad" is the limit that is reached. A parallel to it is His statement the Exalted: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 38].

Know that the meaning of this wish is clear, whether we take the word "amad" to refer to time or to place, since the intended meaning is wishing for its distance. Then He said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, and this is to emphasize the threat. Then He said: ﴿And Allah is Most Kind to the servants﴾, and concerning it there are several views:

The first: He is Most Kind to them in that He warned them of Himself, made them know the perfection of His knowledge and power, and that He gives respite and does not neglect. He encouraged them to earn His mercy and warned them against deserving His wrath. Al-Hasan said: "Among His kindness to them is that He warned them of Himself."

The second: He is Most Kind to the servants in that He gave them respite for repentance, for making amends, and for rectification.

The third: when He said ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, which is for the threat, He followed it with His statement ﴿And Allah is Most Kind to the servants﴾, which is for the promise, so that the servant knows that His promise and mercy prevail over His threat and anger.

The fourth: the word "servants" (al-'ibad) in the Qur'an is specific. He the Exalted said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], and He said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. So the meaning is that when He mentioned the threat against the disbelievers and the rebellious, He mentioned the promise to the people of obedience, saying: ﴿And Allah is Most Kind to the servants﴾, meaning: just as He is avenging against the rebellious, He is Most Kind to the obedient and the good-doers.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 31:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: If you love God, then follow me; God will love you and forgive you your sins. God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Know that when God called the people to belief in Him and belief in His messengers by way of threat and warning, He called them to that by another route, which is that the Jews used to say, ﴿We are the sons of God and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], so this verse was revealed. It is also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) stood over the Quraysh while they were in the Sacred Mosque prostrating to idols, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by God, you have deviated from the religion (millah) of Abraham." The Quraysh said: "We only worship these out of love for God, that they may bring us near to God in closeness," so this verse was revealed. It is also related that the Christians said: "We only exalt the Messiah out of love for God," so this verse was revealed. In sum, every group of rational people claims that it loves God and seeks His pleasure and obedience. So He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): "Say: If you are truthful in your claim to love God, then be submissive to His commands and cautious of disobeying Him." The implied meaning of the statement is: whoever loves God the Exalted must be in the utmost caution regarding what brings about His wrath. When the decisive proof for the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) is established, following him becomes obligatory. If this following does not take place, that indicates that the love in question was not actually present.

Regarding the verse, there are several issues:

The first issue: As for a comprehensive discussion of love, it was already covered in the explanation of His words, ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165]. The theologians (mutakallimun) insist that the love of God the Exalted is an expression for the love of His magnification and exaltation, or the love of obedience to Him, or the love of His reward. They said: because love is of the same kind as will (iradah), and will has no connection except to things that happen (hawadith) and to benefits.

Know that this view is weak, because it is not possible to say of everything that it is loved only for the sake of some other meaning; otherwise there would be an infinite regress (tasalsul) or circularity (dawr). Therefore one must arrive at something that is loved for its own essence. Just as we know that pleasure is loved for its own sake, so too we know that perfection is loved for its own sake. Likewise, when we hear the accounts of Rustam and Isfandiyar in their bravery, the heart inclines toward them, even though we are certain that there is no benefit for us in that inclination; rather, we may even believe that this love is a sin which we are not permitted to persist in. So we know that perfection is loved for its own sake, just as pleasure is loved for its own sake. The perfection of perfections belongs to God the Exalted, so this requires that He be loved for His own essence, by Himself and by those who are near to Him, to whom a trace of the traces of His perfection and majesty has become manifest.

The theologians said: As for the love of God the Exalted for the servant, it is an expression for His will to bring good things and benefits in religion and in this world to him.

The second issue: The people claimed that they were lovers of God the Exalted, and they used to show their desire that God the Exalted would love them. The verse contains the obligation in two respects:

One of them: "If you love God, then follow me," because the miracles have shown that He the Exalted has made it obligatory upon you to follow me. The second: "If you wish that God would love you, then follow me," because when you follow me you have obeyed God, and God the Exalted loves everyone who obeys Him. Also, in following me there is nothing but that I have called you to the obedience of God the Exalted, to exalting Him, and to abandoning the exaltation of other than Him. And whoever loves God is inclined toward Him, because love necessitates turning wholly toward the beloved and turning wholly away from what is not beloved.

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) delved in this context into disparaging the friends of God the Exalted, and wrote here what no rational person should write, the like of which is not fitting even in books of obscenity. Granting that he dared to disparage the friends of God the Exalted, how did he dare to write such obscene speech in the interpretation of the speech of God the Exalted? We ask God for protection and guidance.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿and He will forgive you your sins﴾. What is meant by God's love for the servant is His giving him reward, and by the forgiveness of his sin is the removal of punishment, and this is the utmost that every rational person seeks. Then He said: ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: Forgiving in this world, Who covers over for the servant the various kinds of sins, and Merciful in the Hereafter by His bounty and generosity.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾

It is narrated that when His saying was revealed: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you﴾, and so on, ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy said: "Muhammad makes his obedience like the obedience of Allah, and he commands us to love him as the Christians loved ʿIsa." So this verse was revealed. The explanation of the matter is that when the first verse required following him, the hypocrite cast a doubt into the religion, namely that Muhammad claims for himself what the Christians say about ʿIsa. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned this verse to remove that doubt, saying: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾. That is: Allah has only made it obligatory upon you to follow me, not as the Christians say about ʿIsa, but because I am a Messenger from Allah. Since the one who conveys the obligations from Allah is the Messenger, it follows that his obedience is obligatory. Thus the obligation of following him is for this meaning, not because of the doubts which the hypocrite cast into the religion.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾ That is: if they turn away, then the love of Allah will not be attained by them, because He, exalted is He, has only made praise and commendation obligatory for the one who obeys Him, while the one who disbelieves deserves humiliation and disgrace, and that is the opposite of love. And Allah knows best.

Page 18

Allah Most High said: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds﴾ ﴿offspring, one of whom is from another. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾.

Know that when Allah Most High explained that His love is not complete except by following the messengers, He explained the high ranks of the messengers and the nobility of their positions, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam﴾. In this verse there are several issues.

The first issue: Know that created beings are of two kinds: the mukallaf (those morally accountable, who bear religious obligations) and the non-mukallaf. They agreed that the mukallaf is superior to the non-mukallaf. They agreed that the categories of the mukallaf are four: the angels, humans, jinn, and devils (shayatin). As for the angels, it has been transmitted in reports that Allah created them from wind. Some have argued for the soundness of this by rational arguments:

The first: for this reason they were able to fly at the swiftest speeds.

The second: for this reason they were able to carry the Throne, because wind is what carries things.

The third: for this reason they were called ruhaniyyun (spiritual beings). Another report says that they were created from light, and for this reason they are pure and sincere toward Allah Most High. The better view is to combine the two statements, so we say: their bodies are from wind and their spirits are from light. These are the inhabitants of the realm of the heavens.

As for the devils, they are disbelievers. As for Iblis, his disbelief is evident from the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And he was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34]. As for the rest of the devils, they too are disbelievers, by the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you, and if you obey them, you are indeed polytheists﴾ [al-Anʿam: 121]. Among the distinctive features of the devils is that they are all enemies of humankind. Allah Most High said: ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. And He said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-Anʿam: 112]. Among the distinctive features of the devils is that they were created from fire. Allah Most High said, relating about Iblis: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 12]. And He said: ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of scorching winds﴾ [al-Hijr: 27]. As for the jinn, some of them are disbelievers and some are believers. Allah Most High said: ﴿And among us are the Muslims, and among us are the deviators. Whoever has submitted, those have sought out right guidance﴾ [al-Jinn: 14]. As for humans, there is no doubt that they have a first parent, who is their first father; otherwise it would regress infinitely. The Qur'an indicates that this first one is Adam (ﷺ), as Allah Most High said in this surah: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus to Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al ʿImran: 59]. And He said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate﴾ [al-Nisa': 1].

Having known this, we say: the scholars agreed that humans are superior to jinn and devils. They differed on whether humans are superior to angels. We have thoroughly investigated this issue in the commentary on the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿Prostrate to Adam, so they prostrated﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34].

* * *

Those who hold that humans are superior relied on this verse, because al-istifa' (choosing and selecting) indicates greater honor and elevated rank. So when Allah Most High explained that He chose Adam and his descendants among the prophets over all the worlds, it must be that they are superior to the angels, since they are of the worlds.

If it is said: if we take this verse to mean the preference of the named individuals over all the worlds, it leads to contradiction. Because if a large group is described as each one of them being superior to all the worlds, it entails that each one of them is superior to each other, and that is impossible. If we take it to mean that he was the most excellent of the worlds of his time or of his kind, no contradiction arises. So it is necessary to interpret it in this sense to avoid contradiction. Also, Allah Most High said about the Children of Israel: ﴿And that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 47], and this does not imply that they are superior to Muhammad (ﷺ). Rather, we say that what is meant is the worlds of each one's own time. The answer is clear: in His saying "chose Adam over the worlds," it encompasses everything to which the word "world" can properly be applied, so it includes the angel. At most, the general wording was set aside in some cases by a proof that established this, so we may not set it aside in the remaining cases without a proof.

* * *

The second issue: iṣṭafā (اصطفى) in the language means "chose." So the meaning of "iṣṭafāhum" is that He made them the elite (ṣafwa) of His creation, by way of illustration with what is observed of a thing that is purified and cleansed of turbidity. It is used in three forms: ṣafwa, ṣufwa, and ṣifwa. A parallel to this verse is His saying to Moses: ﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 144]. And about Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob He said: ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the best﴾ [Sad: 47].

Having known this, we say: there are two views concerning the verse. The first: the meaning is that Allah chose the religion of Adam and the religion of Noah, so the choosing refers to their religion, their law, and their creed, and this meaning is on the assumption that a noun has been omitted. The second: that the meaning is that Allah chose them, i.e., purified them from blameworthy qualities and adorned them with praiseworthy traits. This view is preferable for two reasons. The first: we do not need to posit an implied word here. The second: it agrees with His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-Anʿam: 124].

Al-Halimi mentioned in his book "al-Minhaj" that the prophets, peace be upon them, must differ from others in their bodily faculties and their spiritual faculties. As for the bodily faculties, they are either perceptive or motive.

As for the perceptive faculties, they are either outward senses or inward senses. The outward senses are five. The first is the faculty of sight. The Messenger (ﷺ) was specially endowed with perfection in this quality, and two things indicate this:

The first: his saying (ﷺ): "The earth was folded up for me, and I was shown its east and its west."

The second: his saying (ﷺ): "Straighten your rows and close the gaps, for I see you from behind my back."

A parallel to this faculty is what was given to Abraham (ﷺ), namely His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Anʿam: 75]. They said in its interpretation that Allah strengthened his sight until he witnessed all of the dominion, both above and below. Al-Halimi said, may Allah have mercy on him: This is not far-fetched, because people differ in sharpness of sight. It is reported that Zarqa' al-Yamama could see a thing from a distance of three days' travel, so it is not unlikely that the sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) was stronger than hers.

The second: the faculty of hearing. The Prophet (ﷺ) was the strongest of people in this faculty, and two things indicate this:

One of them: his saying (ﷺ): "The heaven creaked, and it had the right to creak; there is not a space the size of a foot in it without an angel prostrating to Allah Most High." So he heard the creaking of the heaven.

The second: that "he heard a rumbling and mentioned that it was the fall of a rock thrown into Hell, which has not yet reached its bottom until now." Al-Halimi said: The philosophers have no way to deny this, for they claimed that Pythagoras trained himself until he heard the faint sound of the celestial sphere. A parallel to this faculty is what Solomon (peace be upon him) had in the story of the ant: ﴿A small ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings"﴾ [al-Naml: 18]. So Allah made Solomon hear the speech of the ant and made him understand its meaning. This also falls under strengthening understanding, and this was granted to Muhammad (ﷺ) when he spoke with the wolf and with the camel.

The third: strengthening the faculty of smell, as in the case of Jacob (peace be upon him), for when Joseph (peace be upon him) ordered that his shirt be carried to him and cast over his face, and when the caravan departed, Jacob said: ﴿Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph﴾ [Yusuf: 94]. He sensed it from a distance of several days.

The fourth: strengthening the faculty of taste, as in the case of our Messenger (ﷺ) when he said: "Indeed this foreleg tells me that it is poisoned."

The fifth: strengthening the faculty of touch, as in the case of the Friend (Abraham), when Allah Most High made the fire cool and safe for him. How then is this considered far-fetched, when something like it is observed in the salamander and the ostrich? As for the inward senses, among them is the faculty of memory. Allah Most High said: ﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ [al-Aʿla: 6]. Among them is the faculty of intelligence. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me a thousand doors of knowledge, and from each door I derived a thousand doors." If this is the state of a walī (friend of Allah), what then is the state of the Prophet (ﷺ)?

As for the motive faculties: such as the Prophet's (ﷺ) ascent to the Mi'raj, the bodily ascent of Jesus to heaven, and the raising up of Enoch (Idris) and Elijah (Ilyas), as reported in the traditions. Allah Most High said: ﴿He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you"﴾ [al-Naml: 40].

As for the rational spiritual faculties: they must be in the utmost perfection and the highest purity.

Know that the complete discussion on this subject is that the holy prophetic soul differs in its essence from all other souls. Among the necessary qualities of that soul are perfection in intelligence, acuteness, freedom, elevation, and transcendence above corporeal things and desires. When the spirit is in the utmost purity and nobility, and the body is in the utmost cleanness and purity, these perceptive and motive faculties are in the utmost perfection, because they function like lights overflowing from the essence of the spirit and reaching the body. Whenever the agent and the recipient are in the utmost perfection, the effects are in the utmost strength, nobility, and purity.

Having known this, His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾ means: Allah Most High chose Adam, either from the inhabitants of the lower world according to the view of those who say that the angel is superior to the human, or from the inhabitants of the higher world according to the view of those who say that the human is the noblest of created beings. Then He placed the perfection of the spiritual faculty in a specific branch of Adam's offspring, namely Seth (Shith) and his descendants, down to Enoch (Idris), then to Noah, then to Abraham. Then from Abraham two branches came forth: Ishmael and Isaac. He made Ishmael the origin of the manifestation of the holy spirit in Muhammad (ﷺ), and He made Isaac the origin of two branches: Jacob and Esau. He placed prophethood in the descendants of Jacob, and He placed kingship in the descendants of Esau. This continued until the time of Muhammad (ﷺ). When Muhammad (ﷺ) appeared, the light of prophethood and the light of kingship were transferred to Muhammad (ﷺ), and both remained, I mean religion and kingship, for his followers until the Resurrection. Whoever reflects on this subject will reach wondrous secrets.

* * *

The third issue: Some people said: the intended meaning of "the family of Abraham" is the believers, as in His saying: ﴿The Fire, to which they are exposed﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. The correct view is that what is meant by them is the descendants, and they are the ones intended by His saying: ﴿Indeed I will make you an imam for the people." He said, "And of my descendants?" He said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. As for "the family of ʿImran," scholars have differed about it. Some said: what is meant is ʿImran, the father of Moses and Aaron, who was ʿImran son of Yashhar son of Qahath son of Levi son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham. So the family of ʿImran would mean Moses, Aaron, and their followers among the prophets. Others said: rather, what is meant is ʿImran son of Matthan, the father of Mary, who was of the lineage of Solomon son of David son of Jesse, and they were of the lineage of Judah son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham, peace be upon them. They said: between the two ʿImrans there are one thousand eight hundred years. Those who held this view argued for its soundness with several matters.

The first: that the one mentioned right after His saying: ﴿and the family of ʿImran over the worlds﴾ is ʿImran son of Matthan, the maternal grandfather of Jesus (peace be upon him), so it is more appropriate to direct the speech to him.

Second part of al-Razi's commentary (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verses 33–37:

Secondly: the purpose of the discourse is that the Christians were arguing for the divinity of Jesus on the basis of the extraordinary events that appeared at his hands. Thus God, exalted is He, says: these things appeared at his hands only as an honour from God, exalted is He, bestowed upon him, because He chose him over the worlds and singled him out with great honours. Therefore, it is more fitting in this context to take this discourse as referring to ʿImran ibn Mathan than to take it as referring to ʿImran, the father of Moses and Aaron.

Thirdly: this expression is very closely matched by God's words: ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:91]. Know that these points are not strong proofs; rather, they are speculative matters, and the basic possibility remains.

* * *

As for God's words: ﴿offspring, one from another﴾, there are two issues concerning it.

The first issue: concerning the grammatical case of His words "dhurriyyatan" (offspring), there are two views:
The first: it is a substitute (badal) for "the family of Abraham."
The second: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: He chose them while some of them were from others.

The second issue: concerning the interpretation of the verse, there are several views:
The first: "offspring, some of whom are from others" in monotheism, sincerity and obedience. A parallel is God's words: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], this being due to their sharing in hypocrisy.
The second: "offspring, some of whom are from others" in the sense that those other than Adam (peace be upon him) were born from Adam (peace be upon him), and the intended meaning of "offspring" is those other than Adam.

As for God's words: ﴿And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:224], al-Qaffal said: the meaning is that God hears the words of His servants and knows their inward thoughts and deeds, and He chooses from His creation only the one whom He knows to be upright in word and deed. A parallel is God's words: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 6:124], and His words: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good works, and they would call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humble before Us﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:90]. There is another view: the Jews used to say, "We are the descendants of Abraham and of the family of ʿImran, so we are the sons of God and His beloved." The Christians used to say, "The Messiah is the son of God." Some of them knew that this statement was false, but to comfort the hearts of the common people they remained insistent upon it. So God, as if He were saying: "God hears these false statements of yours and knows the corrupt aims behind these statements, and He will requite you for them." Thus the beginning of the verse is a declaration of the nobility of the prophets and messengers, and its end is a threat to these liars who claim that they are firmly upon their religions.

Know that after this verse God mentions many narratives:

* * *

The first narrative:
The event of Hannah, mother of Mary (peace be upon them both): ﴿When the wife of ʿImran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿And when she gave birth to her, she said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and God knew best what she had given birth to, "and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from the accursed Satan."﴾ ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow in a goodly way, and entrusted her to Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found provision with her. He said: "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She said: "It is from God. Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning."﴾

Page 22

The words of God: ﴿When the wife of ʿImran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿And when she gave birth to her, she said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and God knew best what she had given birth to, "and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from the accursed Satan."﴾ ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow in a goodly way, and entrusted her to Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found provision with her. He said: "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She said: "It is from God. Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning."﴾.

There are issues concerning this:

The first issue: concerning the grammatical position of "idh" (when) there are several views. The first: Abu ʿUbayda said it is a superfluous particle with no place in the grammar, and the meaning is: "the wife of ʿImran said." Al-Zajjaj said: Abu ʿUbayda did not do well in this, because it is not permissible to nullify a letter of the Book of God, nor to omit a letter of the Book of God without necessity.

The second: al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad said: the implied meaning is "remember when the wife of ʿImran said," and similar usage is abundant in the Book of God. The third: al-Zajjaj said the implied meaning is: "and He chose the family of ʿImran over the worlds when the wife of ʿImran said." Ibn al-Anbari objected to this, saying: God has linked the choosing of the family of ʿImran with the choosing of Adam and Noah, and since God's choosing of Adam and Noah occurred before the statement of the wife of ʿImran, it is impossible to say that this choosing is restricted to that time in which the wife of ʿImran made this statement. It may be answered that the effect of each one's election appeared when he came into existence and his obedience appeared, so it is permissible to say that God chose Adam upon his existence, Noah upon his existence, and the family of ʿImran when the wife of ʿImran made this statement.

The fourth: some said this is connected to what precedes it, and the implied meaning is: "God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing when the wife of ʿImran made this statement." If it is said: God was All-Hearing and All-Knowing before the woman made this statement, so what is the meaning of this restriction? We say: His hearing of that speech is restricted to the existence of that speech, and His knowledge that she would mention it is restricted to her mentioning it; change in knowledge and hearing occurs only in relations and related objects.

The second issue: Zechariah son of Adhan and ʿImran son of Mathan lived in the same era. The wife of ʿImran was Hannah daughter of Faqudh, and Zechariah had married her daughter Ishaʿ, the sister of Mary, and Yahya and ʿIsa (peace be upon them both) were maternal cousins. Then, concerning the manner of this vow, there are narrations:

The first narration: ʿIkrima said: she was barren and could not bear children, and she used to envy women for their children. Then she said: "O God, I vow to You that if You grant me a child, I will dedicate him in charity to Jerusalem so that he may serve in it."

The second narration: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the mother of Mary had no child until she grew old. One day she was in the shade of a tree and saw a bird feeding its chick, and her soul was stirred toward having a child. So she called upon her Lord to grant her a child, and she conceived Mary. ʿImran died, and when she realized (her pregnancy), she dedicated the child to God as a muharrar, that is, a servant of the mosque. al-Hasan al-Basri said: she only did this by inspiration from God, and without it she would not have done so, just as Abraham saw in a dream the slaughter of his son and knew that this was a command from God even though it was not by revelation, and just as God inspired the mother of Moses so that she cast him into the river, and that was not by revelation.

The third issue: the muharrar is one who is made free, pure, and unmixed. It is said: "I freed the slave" when you delivered him from bondage; "I freed the writing" when you corrected and purified it so that no trace of error remains in it; a "free man" is one who belongs wholly to himself with no one having a claim upon him; and "free clay" is clay pure of sand, stones, mud and defects.

As for the interpretation, it has been said: devoted purely to worship, according to al-Shaʿbi. It has been said: a servant of the church. It has been said: freed from worldly affairs for the obedience of God. It has been said: a servant of one who teaches the Book and instructs in the churches. The meaning is that she vowed to make that child a dedicated endowment for the obedience of God. Al-Asamm said: the children of Israel had no spoils of war or captives, so their freeing was making their children in the manner we have described. This is because in their religion, when a child became capable of being employed, he was obliged to serve his parents; so by vow they would forgo that kind of benefit and make them muharrarun for the service of the mosque and the obedience of God. It has also been said: the muharrar would be placed in the church to serve it until he reached puberty, then he would be given the choice between remaining and leaving; if he chose to leave he could leave, and if he chose to remain he would have no option afterward. And there was no prophet except that among his descendants there was a muharrar in Jerusalem.

The fourth issue: this freeing was permissible only for boys; as for girls, they were not fit for it because of menstruation and harm that befalls them. Yet Hannah vowed absolutely, either because she built the matter on supposition, or because she made that vow a means of seeking a male child.

The fifth issue: concerning the accusative of His words "muharraran" (dedicated), there are two views. The first: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "ma" (what), and its implied meaning is: "I have vowed to You that which is in my womb as a dedicated one." The second, which is the view of Ibn Qutayba: the meaning is "I have vowed to You that I will make what is in my womb a dedicated one."

Then God, relating her words, said: ﴿So accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ Taqabbul (acceptance) means taking a thing with approval. al-Wahidi said: its root is from "muqabala" (correspondence), because it is returned with reward. This is the speech of one who intends by what she did only the seeking of God's pleasure and sincerity in His worship. Then she said: ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, and the meaning is: Indeed You are the All-Hearing of my supplication, my calling and my pleading, the All-Knowing of what is in my heart, my soul and my intention.

Know that this kind of vow existed in the law of the children of Israel and does not exist in our law, and laws may differ in such rulings.

God said: ﴿So when she gave birth to her.﴾ Know that this pronoun either refers to the female who was in her womb, and she knew that it was a female; or it is said that it refers to the soul and the living being; or it is said that it refers to the dedicated one.

* * *

Then God said: ﴿She said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female."﴾ Know that the benefit of this statement is that she had previously made the vow concerning the freeing of what was in her womb, and her strong supposition was that it would be a male, so she did not stipulate that in her speech. And it was the custom among them that the one who is freed and set aside for service to the mosque and the obedience of God is the male, not the female. So she said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," fearing that her vow had not fallen into the position on which it could be relied, and apologizing for her previous unrestricted vow. She mentioned this not as an informing of God,

Page 24

exalted is He, for God is far above needing to be informed by her; rather she mentioned it by way of apology.

Then God said: ﴿And God knew best what she had given birth to.﴾ Abu Bakr, from ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir read "wada'tu" with a raised tāʾ (wa ḍaʿtu), as the quotation of her words. The benefit of this discourse is that when she said: "I have given birth to a female," she feared that it might be thought she was informing God, so she removed the doubt by saying: "And God knew best what she had given birth to." And it is established that she said that as an apology, not as an informing. The rest read it with a jazm (wa ḍaʿat), on the basis that it is God's speech. On this reading the meaning is that He, exalted is He, said: "And God knew best what she had given birth to," magnifying her child and making her ignorant of the greatness of that child; its meaning is: God knows best the thing she gave birth to and the great matters attached to it, and that He would make him and his son a sign for the worlds, while she was ignorant of that and knew nothing of it, and therefore she was grieved. In the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas, "wa-llahu aʿlamu bima waḍaʿt" (with a sukun on the tāʾ, addressing her), that is: you do not know the value of this bestowed one, while God is the one who knows its wonders and signs.

Then God, relating her words, said: ﴿and the male is not like the female.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: her intention was to prefer the male child over the female, and there are several reasons for this preference.

The first of them: their law did not permit dedicating males without females.

[Page 25]

The second: the male is able to continue serving the place of worship, and this is not valid for the female because of menstruation and the other conditions particular to women.

The third: the male, because of his strength and vigour, is suited to service, unlike the female, who is weak and cannot bear service.

The fourth: the male does not suffer any blemish in serving and mixing with people, whereas the female does.

The fifth: the male does not incur the suspicion that falls upon the female when mixing with others. These aspects therefore require the superiority of the male over the female in this respect.

The second view: the purpose of this statement is to prefer this female over the male. It is as if she said: "The male is what I sought, but this female is a gift from God Most High. The male I sought is not like the female who is a gift to God." This statement indicates that this woman was absorbed in knowing the majesty of God, aware that what the Lord does for the servant is better than what the servant wants for himself.

* * *

Then God Most High related a second statement from her, which is her saying: ﴿And I have named her Maryam﴾. Concerning it there are several discussions:

The first discussion: the apparent meaning of this statement indicates what we have related, that Imran had died while Hannah was carrying Maryam. Therefore the mother took charge of naming her, since it is customary for fathers to undertake this.

The second discussion: Maryam, in their language, means "the worshipper." By this name she wished to ask God Most High to protect her from the calamities of religion and of the world. What confirms this is her saying afterwards: ﴿And I seek refuge for her and her offspring with You from the accursed Satan﴾.

The third discussion: His saying ﴿And I have named her Maryam﴾ means: "I have named her with this word," that is, I made this word her name. This indicates that the name, the named, and the act of naming are three distinct things.

Then God Most High related a third statement from her, which is her saying: ﴿And I seek refuge for her and her offspring with You from the accursed Satan﴾. This was because, when what she had wished for, that it be a boy serving the mosque, had escaped her, she humbly turned to God Most High asking that He preserve her from the accursed Satan and make her among the righteous, devout women. The explanation of "the accursed Satan" has already been given at the beginning of the book.

* * *

When God Most High related these words of Hannah, He said: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾. Concerning it there are two questions:

The first question: He said ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾ and did not say "accepted her with an acceptance" (taqabbul). This is because qabul and taqabbul are close in meaning. God Most High said: ﴿And God has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾ [Nuh: 17], meaning "a causing to grow." Qabul is the verbal noun of the saying "so-and-so accepted the thing (qabila al-shay') with acceptance (qabulan)" when he was pleased with it. Sibawayh said: five verbal nouns came in the pattern fa'ul: qabul, tahur, wudu', wuqud, and wulug, except that for wuqud as a verbal noun the more common form is with a damma. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj permitted qubul with a damma. Tha'lab related from Ibn al-A'rabi that it is said: "I received it, qabulan and qubulan." There is another aspect in the verse: whatever belongs to the pattern tafa''ul indicates the intense concern of the doer with showing that action, as in tasabbur (forcing oneself to be patient) and tajallud (showing fortitude) and the like, for these two convey earnestness in showing patience and endurance. Likewise here, taqabbul conveys exaggeration in showing acceptance.

If it is said: "Why did He not say 'accepted her with a good taqabbul' so that the exaggeration would be more complete?"

The answer: although the word taqabbul conveys what we have mentioned, it conveys a kind of effort against nature. As for qabul, it conveys the meaning of acceptance in accordance with nature. So He mentioned taqabbul to convey earnestness and exaggeration, then mentioned qabul to convey that this is not against nature but in accordance with nature. And although these aspects are inapplicable in relation to God Most High, they indicate by way of metaphor the occurrence of great care in her upbringing. This aspect is appropriate and rationally sound.

The second question: the commentators mentioned several aspects concerning that good acceptance.

The first aspect: God Most High protected her and protected her son Jesus, peace be upon him, from the touch of Satan. Abu Hurayrah related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every child that is born is touched by Satan at the moment of birth, so it cries out loudly from the touch of Satan, except Maryam and her son." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿And I seek refuge for her and her offspring with You from Satan﴾." The judge (al-Qadi) criticized this report and said: it is a solitary report (khabar wahid) contrary to the evidence, so it must be rejected. We say it is contrary to the evidence for several reasons:

One: Satan only invites to evil those who know good and evil, and the child is not like that.

Two: if Satan were able to poke in this way, he would do more than that, by destroying the righteous and corrupting their conditions.

Three: why were Maryam and Jesus, peace be upon them both, singled out for this exception, rather than the rest of the prophets, peace be upon them?

Four: if that prodding existed, its effect would remain, and if its effect remained, the crying and weeping would continue. Since that is not the case, we know its falsehood. Know that these reasons are open to interpretation, and a report cannot be rejected on the basis of such considerations. And God knows best.

The second aspect, concerning the meaning of God Most High accepting her with a good acceptance: it was reported that when Hannah gave birth to Maryam, she wrapped her in a cloth, carried her to the mosque, and placed her with the rabbis, the sons of Aaron, who in Bayt al-Maqdis were like the keepers (hajabah) of the Ka'bah. She said: "Take this votive offering (nadhirah)." They competed for her, because she was the daughter of their leader. The sons of Mathan were the chiefs, rabbis and kings of the Children of Israel. Zakariyya said to them: "I have the greatest right to her, since her aunt is with me." They said: "No, until we draw lots over her." So they went, and they were twenty-seven, to a river, and cast into it their pens with which they used to write the revelation, on the condition that whoever's pen rose would be the one who wins. Then they cast their pens three times, and each time Zakariyya's pen rose above the water while theirs sank, so Zakariyya took her.

The third aspect: al-Qaffal related from al-Hasan that he said: Maryam spoke in her childhood just as the Messiah spoke, and she never took the breast, and her provision used to come to her from Paradise.

The fourth aspect, concerning the good acceptance: the custom in that law was that dedication (tahrir) was permitted only for a boy when he became mature and capable of serving the mosque. Here, when God Most High knew the humble supplication of that woman, He accepted that girl while she was young and unable to serve the mosque. All of this constitutes the aspects mentioned in explaining the good acceptance.

Then God Most High said: ﴿And He caused her to grow with a good growth﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: the implied meaning is "He caused her to grow, so she grew with a good growth." Then some interpreted this good growth as relating to worldly matters, and others interpreted it as relating to religious matters. As for the first, they said: the meaning is that she used to grow in a day as much as a child grows in a year. As for religion, it is because she grew in righteousness, uprightness, chastity and obedience.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾. Concerning it there are two questions:

The first question: it is said: kafala, yakfulu, kafalatan and kaflan, so he is a kafil (guardian), who is one who spends upon a person and takes care of his affairs. In a hadith: "I and the one who cares for an orphan are like these two." And God Most High said: ﴿Entrust her to me﴾ [Sad: 23].

The second question: 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "wa-kaffala-ha" with shaddah. Then they differed concerning Zakariyya: 'Asim read it with the long vowel (Zakariyyā'), while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the short vowel (Zakariyya), in the sense that God Most High joined her to Zakariyya. Whoever reads "Zakariyyā'" with the long vowel shows the accusative case explicitly, and whoever reads with the short vowel is in the position of the accusative. The rest read with the long vowel and the nominative, in the sense that Zakariyya joined her to himself, and this is the preferred reading, because it is appropriate to God's saying: ﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44], and most scholars hold it. It is related from Ibn Kathir in one narration "kafila-ha" with a kasrah on the fa'. As for the short and long vowel in Zakariyya, they are two dialects, like al-Haija' and al-Haija. Mujahid read "fa-taqabbal-ha rabbu-ha, wa-anbit-ha, wa-kaffil-ha" with the imperative form in the three verbs and the accusative on "rabba-ha," as if she were supplicating God, saying: "Accept her, O her Lord; cause her to grow, O her Lord; and make Zakariyya her guardian."

The third question: the scholars differed about when Zakariyya, peace be upon him, took charge of her. Most said it was during her infancy, and the reports come with this. Some said that he only took charge of her after she was weaned. They argued for this with two points. The first: God Most High said: ﴿And He caused her to grow with a good growth﴾, then said: ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾, and this suggests that the guardianship came after that good growth. The second: God Most High said: ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found provision with her. He said: O Maryam, from where is this for you? She said: It is from God﴾, and this indicates that she had already been weaned at the time of that guardianship. Those who held the first view answered that the conjunction "wa" does not necessarily imply sequence, so perhaps the good growth and Zakariyya's guardianship occurred together. As for the second point, perhaps his entering upon her and asking her this question took place at the end of the period of guardianship.

* * *

[Page 26 continues below]

Then God said: ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab), he found provision with her﴾. Concerning it there are several issues:

The first issue: the mihrab is the lofty and noble place. 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah said:

"Mistress of a mihrab, when I came to her, I did not approach until I had climbed a ladder."

Al-Asma'i argued that the mihrab is the upper chamber by God's saying: ﴿When they climbed over the walls into the mihrab﴾ [Sad: 21], and climbing over is only from a height. It was said: the mihrab is the most noble and elevated of assemblies. It is related that when she became a young woman, Zakariyya, peace be upon him, built her a chamber in the mosque, and its door was in its middle, so it could not be ascended except by a ladder. Whenever he left, he would lock seven doors upon her.

The second issue: our companions argued for the validity of the doctrine of the miracles of the saints (karamat al-awliya') from this verse. The basis of the argument is that God Most High informed us that whenever Zakariyya entered the mihrab upon her, he found provision with her. He said: "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She said: "It is from God." The occurrence of that provision with her is either a violation of custom or not. If we say it is not a violation of custom, then this is invalid for five reasons:

First: on this assumption, the occurrence of that provision with Maryam would not be evidence of the elevation of her rank, the nobility of her degree, and her distinction over other people by that特 quality, whereas it is evident that the purpose of the verse is this meaning.

Second: God Most High said after this verse: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord, saying: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38]. The Qur'an indicates that he had despaired of offspring because of his old age and his wife's old age. When he saw the breaking of custom in Maryam's case, he hoped for the birth of a child, so his saying ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38] is consistent. But if what he witnessed in Maryam's case were not a violation of custom, witnessing it would not have been a cause for his hope in the breaking of custom through the birth of a child from an aged, barren woman.

Third: the indefiniteness in His saying ﴿he found provision with her﴾ indicates the magnification of the state of that provision, as if it were said: "a provision," that is, a strange, wondrous provision. This conveys the purpose appropriate to the context of this verse only if it was a violation of custom.

The fourth point: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 91]. Had extraordinary events not appeared at their hands, this would not be valid.

If it is said: why is it not permissible to say that what is meant is that God, exalted is He, created for her a child without a male?

We say: this is not a sign. Rather, its validity would need a sign to establish it. So how could we interpret the verse as referring to that? Rather, what is meant by the sign is that which indicates her truthfulness and purity, and that can only be through the appearance of extraordinary events (khawariq al-'adat) at her hand, as they appeared at the hand of her son 'Isa, peace be upon him.

The fifth point: the reports are widely transmitted that Zakariyya, peace be upon him, would find with her winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter. It is established, then, that what appeared regarding Maryam, peace be upon her, was an act that broke the normal course of things. We say: either it is said that it was a miracle (mu'jizah) of one of the prophets, or it was not so. The first is false, because the prophet present in that time was Zakariyya, peace be upon him. Had that been a miracle for him, he would have known its circumstances and its nature, and so its matter should not have been unclear to him, and he should not have said to Maryam: ﴿Where does this come to you from?﴾. Furthermore, God's saying: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38] indicates that when he asked her about the matter of those things, and she then told him that it was from God, there he hoped for the breaking of the normal course in the birth of a child from a barren, aged, sterile woman. That shows that he did not learn of those circumstances except
[page 28]
except through Maryam's informing him. When the matter is so, it is established that those extraordinary events were not a miracle for Zakariyya, peace be upon him. Nothing remains but to say that they were a karamah (a token of honour, a saintly marvel) for 'Isa, peace be upon him, or a karamah for Maryam, peace be upon her. On either assumption the purpose is achieved. This is the basis of the argument from this verse for the occurrence of the karamat of the awliya' (the friends of God).

Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i (d. 303 AH, a Mu'tazili theologian) objected and said: why is it not permissible to say that those extraordinary events were among the miracles of Zakariyya, peace be upon him? Its explanation is in two respects:

The first: Zakariyya, peace be upon him, prayed for her in general terms that God would bring her provision, and perhaps he was unaware of the details of the provisions that came to her from God, exalted is He. So when he saw a particular thing at a specific time, he said to her: ﴿Where does this come to you from?﴾ She said: ﴿It is from God.﴾ At that point it becomes known that God, through his prayer, manifested that miracle. The second: it is possible that Zakariyya was witnessing with Maryam a customary provision, except that it was coming to her from heaven, and Zakariyya would ask her about it fearing that it might be coming to her from a person whom someone had sent to her. So she said: it is from God, not from anyone else.

The second stance: we do not concede that any of the breaches of the normal course had appeared at Maryam's hand. Rather, the meaning of the verse is that God, exalted is He, had caused provision to reach her through the hands of believers who were eager to spend on pious, devoted women. So whenever Zakariyya, peace be upon him, saw something of that kind, he feared that the provision might have reached her by an improper means, so he would ask her about the circumstances. This is the entirety of what al-Jubba'i said in his interpretation, and it is extremely weak. For if that were a miracle for Zakariyya, peace be upon him, he would have been authorized by God, exalted is He, to seek it, and when he was authorized in that seeking, he would have known with certainty that it would be realized. Once he knew that, it would be impossible for him to ask her about the circumstances. Moreover, God's saying ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38] would also have no purpose. This same answer applies to the second respect.

As for his third question, it is extremely feeble, because on this supposition there remains no reason for Maryam's being singled out for such an event. Furthermore, if there was in his heart the possibility that this provision might have reached her by an improper route, then how, by her mere informing him, could that suspicion be removed? So we know that these questions fall away. And success is from God.

As for the Mu'tazila, they argued against the possibility of karamat, saying: they are indications of the truthfulness of the prophets, and the proof of prophethood does not exist with non-prophets, just as a skilful act, being a proof of knowledge, necessarily does not exist in the case of one who is not knowing.

The answer comes in several respects:

The first: the appearance of an act that breaks the normal course is a proof of the truthfulness of the one who claims. If its bearer claims prophethood, then that extraordinary act indicates that he is a prophet; and if he claims guardianship (wilayah), then it indicates that he is a friend of God.

The second: some of them said: the prophets are commanded to make them manifest, while the friends of God are commanded to conceal them.

The third: a prophet claims the miracle and asserts it with certainty, whereas a friend of God cannot assert it with certainty.

The fourth: a miracle must be free from being opposed by a challenge, whereas a karamah need not be free from being opposed. This is the sum of the discussion on this subject. And success is from God.

Then God, exalted is He, said, recounting of Maryam, peace be upon her: ﴿Indeed God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning.﴾ This may be part of Maryam's speech, and it may be part of the speech of God, glorified and exalted is He. His saying ﴿without reckoning﴾ means: without measure, because of its abundance; or without a request she made in a manner suited to its being granted. This is like His saying: ﴿and He provides for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq: 3]. And here ends the discussion of the story of Hannah.

Allah Most High said: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds﴾ ﴿offspring, one of whom is from another. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾.

Know that when Allah Most High explained that His love is not complete except by following the messengers, He explained the high ranks of the messengers and the nobility of their positions, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam﴾. In this verse there are several issues.

The first issue: Know that created beings are of two kinds: the mukallaf (those morally accountable, who bear religious obligations) and the non-mukallaf. They agreed that the mukallaf is superior to the non-mukallaf. They agreed that the categories of the mukallaf are four: the angels, humans, jinn, and devils (shayatin). As for the angels, it has been transmitted in reports that Allah created them from wind. Some have argued for the soundness of this by rational arguments:

The first: for this reason they were able to fly at the swiftest speeds.

The second: for this reason they were able to carry the Throne, because wind is what carries things.

The third: for this reason they were called ruhaniyyun (spiritual beings). Another report says that they were created from light, and for this reason they are pure and sincere toward Allah Most High. The better view is to combine the two statements, so we say: their bodies are from wind and their spirits are from light. These are the inhabitants of the realm of the heavens.

As for the devils, they are disbelievers. As for Iblis, his disbelief is evident from the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And he was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34]. As for the rest of the devils, they too are disbelievers, by the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you, and if you obey them, you are indeed polytheists﴾ [al-Anʿam: 121]. Among the distinctive features of the devils is that they are all enemies of humankind. Allah Most High said: ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. And He said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-Anʿam: 112]. Among the distinctive features of the devils is that they were created from fire. Allah Most High said, relating about Iblis: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 12]. And He said: ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of scorching winds﴾ [al-Hijr: 27]. As for the jinn, some of them are disbelievers and some are believers. Allah Most High said: ﴿And among us are the Muslims, and among us are the deviators. Whoever has submitted, those have sought out right guidance﴾ [al-Jinn: 14]. As for humans, there is no doubt that they have a first parent, who is their first father; otherwise it would regress infinitely. The Qur'an indicates that this first one is Adam (ﷺ), as Allah Most High said in this surah: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus to Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al ʿImran: 59]. And He said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate﴾ [al-Nisa': 1].

Having known this, we say: the scholars agreed that humans are superior to jinn and devils. They differed on whether humans are superior to angels. We have thoroughly investigated this issue in the commentary on the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿Prostrate to Adam, so they prostrated﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34].

* * *

Those who hold that humans are superior relied on this verse, because al-istifa' (choosing and selecting) indicates greater honor and elevated rank. So when Allah Most High explained that He chose Adam and his descendants among the prophets over all the worlds, it must be that they are superior to the angels, since they are of the worlds.

If it is said: if we take this verse to mean the preference of the named individuals over all the worlds, it leads to contradiction. Because if a large group is described as each one of them being superior to all the worlds, it entails that each one of them is superior to each other, and that is impossible. If we take it to mean that he was the most excellent of the worlds of his time or of his kind, no contradiction arises. So it is necessary to interpret it in this sense to avoid contradiction. Also, Allah Most High said about the Children of Israel: ﴿And that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 47], and this does not imply that they are superior to Muhammad (ﷺ). Rather, we say that what is meant is the worlds of each one's own time. The answer is clear: in His saying "chose Adam over the worlds," it encompasses everything to which the word "world" can properly be applied, so it includes the angel. At most, the general wording was set aside in some cases by a proof that established this, so we may not set it aside in the remaining cases without a proof.
