Then He said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieve﴾. The lam in ﴿That He may cut off a portion﴾ is connected with His saying ﴿And victory is not except from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise﴾. The meaning is that the purpose of your being helped through the support of the angels is that they cut off a portion of those who disbelieve, i.e., destroy a group of them and kill a part of them. It has been said that it refers back to His saying ﴿and that your hearts may be assured thereby﴾, and ﴿That He may cut off a portion﴾ is mentioned without a conjunctive particle, because when one part is close to another part, the conjunction may be omitted. It is like a master saying to his slave: "I honored you so that you would serve me, so that you would help me, so that you would perform my service," with the conjunction omitted, because one part is close to another. Likewise here. His saying ﴿a portion﴾ means a group and a part. The mention of "portion" (taraf) was apt in this context, and the mention of "middle" (wasat) was not apt, because one cannot reach the middle except after taking from the portion. This accords with His saying: ﴿Fight those who are near you of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 123], and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿or subdue them﴾. Al-kabt in the language means throwing a thing down on its face. It is said: "I subdued him, and he was subdued (fa-inkabata)." This is its explanation. Then it is used to mean humiliation, destruction, cursing, defeat, rage, and degradation. The commentators mentioned all of these in explaining al-kabt. His saying ﴿defeated﴾: khaybah is deprivation. The difference between khaybah and yas (despair) is that khaybah occurs only after expectation, whereas yas may occur after expectation and before it. So the opposite of yas is raja' (hope), and the opposite of khaybah is zafar (success). And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as glad tidings for you, and that your hearts may be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieve or subdue them so they return defeated.﴾

[Page 190]

The Almighty said: ﴿Thou hast no part in the affair, whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾.

On this verse there are several questions.

**First question: the occasion of revelation.** There are two views.

The first, which is the well-known one, is that the verse was revealed concerning the Battle of Uhud. Then [Page 191]... no. Continuing: those who hold this view differ in three ways.

The first is that the Prophet ﷺ intended to invoke curses upon the disbelievers, and so this verse was revealed. Those who hold this mention several possibilities. One is that it is reported that Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas struck him, broke his incisor, and he began wiping the blood from his face, while Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, was washing the blood from his face, and he was saying: "How will a people prosper who stained the face of their prophet with blood while he was calling them to their Lord?" Then he wished to invoke curses upon them, and this verse was revealed. The second is what Salim ibn Abd Allah reported from his father Abd Allah ibn Umar: that the Prophet ﷺ cursed some people, saying: "O Allah, curse Abu Sufyan. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿or He turns to them in mercy﴾, so Allah turned in mercy to these people, and their Islam became good. The third is that it was revealed concerning Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, because when the Prophet ﷺ saw him, and saw what they had done to him by mutilation, he said: "I will mutilate thirty of them in return." Then this verse was revealed. Al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: all these things occurred on the day of Uhud, so this verse was revealed concerning all of them, and there is no objection to applying it to all these possibilities.

The second view is that the verse was revealed because the Prophet ﷺ wished to curse the Muslims who disobeyed his command and fled, but Allah prevented him from this. This view is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.

The third way is that the Prophet ﷺ wished to ask forgiveness for the Muslims who fled and disobeyed his command, and to invoke curses upon them, and so the verse was revealed. All these possibilities and views are based on our statement that this verse was revealed concerning the episode of Uhud.

The second view is that it was revealed concerning another event: the Prophet ﷺ sent a group of his best companions to the people of Bi'r Ma'unah to teach them the Qur'an. Amir ibn al-Tufayl went to them with his army, seized them and killed them. The Messenger ﷺ was greatly distressed by this, and he invoked curses upon the disbelievers for forty days, and then this verse was revealed. This is the view of Muqatil, and it is far-fetched, because most scholars agree that this verse concerns the episode of Uhud, the context of the speech indicates it, and placing an unrelated story at the beginning and end of the discourse is not fitting.

* * *

**Second question:** The apparent meaning of this verse indicates that it was revealed concerning a matter in which the Prophet ﷺ was doing something, and this verse was like a prohibition against it. At this point a problem arises: if that action was by the command of Allah, how did Allah prohibit him from it? And if we say it was not by Allah's command and permission, how can this be reconciled with His saying: ﴿nor does he speak from desire﴾ [al-Najm 53:3]? Also, the verse indicates the infallibility (ismah) of the prophets, peace be upon them. So if the thing prohibited in this verse was good, why did Allah forbid it? And if it was wrong, how can its doer be infallible?

The answer comes in several ways.

The first: the prohibition from an act does not indicate that the one prohibited was engaged in it. Allah said to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿If you were to associate partners with Allah, your deeds would surely be lost﴾ [al-Zumar 39:65], while he, peace be upon him, never associated partners with Allah. And He said: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:1], which does not indicate that he did not fear Allah. Then He said: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:1], and this does not indicate that he obeyed them. The benefit of this prohibition is that when something occurred that caused great grief and intense anger, namely the mutilation of his uncle Hamzah and the killing of the Muslims, and it is apparent that anger drives a person to what is not fitting of speech and action, then, so that the sight of those hateful things would not lead him to what is unbecoming in speech and action, Allah explicitly forbade it, to strengthen his infallibility and to affirm his purity.

The second: perhaps he, peace be upon him, did it, but it was a matter of leaving what is superior and preferable (al-afdal wa al-awla). So Allah guided him to choose what is superior and preferable. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of what you were made to suffer. But if you endure patiently, it is better for the patient﴾ [al-Nahl 16:126]. ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 16:127]. It is as if He said: if you are going to punish that wrongdoer, then be content with the equivalent. Then He said a second time: if you leave him, that is better. Then He commanded him with a firm command to leave him, saying: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 16:127].

The third answer: perhaps when his heart inclined toward cursing them, he sought permission from his Lord concerning it, and so Allah explicitly prohibited him from it. On this assumption, this prohibition does not indicate any flaw in his infallibility.

* * *

**Third question:** His saying ﴿Thou hast no part in the affair﴾ has two views.

The first is that its meaning is: you have no share in the matter of this event or in the affair of this incident. Regarding this, statements have been transmitted from the commentators. One is: you have no share in the interests of My servants except what has been revealed to you. The second: you have no share in the question of their destruction, because He is more knowing of the interests, and perhaps He will turn to them in mercy. The third: you have no say in whether Allah turns to them in mercy, nor in whether He punishes them.

The second view is that what is meant is the command that is opposed to a prohibition, and the meaning is: you have no share in the command concerning My creation except when it is in accordance with My command. This is like His saying: ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾ [al-An'am 6:57] and His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾ [al-Rum 30:4].

On both views, the purpose of the verse is to prohibit him, peace be upon him, from every act and speech except what is by his permission and command. This is the guidance to the highest stations of servanthood (ubudiyyah). Then they differed about the reason for the prohibition from cursing. Some said that its wisdom is that Allah perhaps knew of some of the disbelievers that they would repent, or, even if they did not repent, He knew that a child would be born from them who would be a Muslim, righteous and pious. Whoever is like this, the fitting thing for Allah's mercy is to grant him respite in this world and to ward off calamities from him until he repents or until that child is born. So if the Prophet's invocation for their destruction were answered, that aim would be lost; and if his invocation were not answered, that would be like belittling the Messenger ﷺ. For this reason Allah forbade him from cursing and commanded him to entrust everything to Allah's knowledge.

Others said: its purpose is to show the powerlessness of servanthood, and that the servant should not delve into the secrets of Allah in His dominion and His sovereignty. This is the best view in my opinion, and the most consistent with knowing the principles that indicate the reality of lordship (rububiyyah) and servanthood.

**Fourth question:** Al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and others mentioned two views concerning this verse.

The first: His saying ﴿or He turns to them in mercy﴾ is coordinated (ma'tuf) with what precedes it. The sense is: that He might cut off a part of those who disbelieved, or humiliate them, or turn to them in mercy, or punish them. And His saying ﴿Thou hast no part in the affair﴾ is like an unrelated statement lying between the coordinated element and that to which it is coordinated, as you say: "I struck Zayd, so inform Amr of that." On this view, this verse is connected to what came before it.

The second view: the meaning of "or" (aw) here is the meaning of "until" (hatta), or "unless" (illa an), as in your saying: "I will surely cling to you until you give me my right," meaning: "unless you give me" or "until you give me." The sense of the verse is: you have no part in their affair except that Allah turns to them in mercy, so that you rejoice in their state, or that He punishes them, so that you are satisfied with them.

* * *

**Fifth question:** His saying ﴿or He turns to them in mercy﴾ is explained by our companions (the Ash'ari scholars) as Allah creating repentance (tawbah) in them. That is an expression for creating in them regret for what has passed, and creating in them a resolve not to do the like of it in the future. Our companions said: this meaning is confirmed by the proof of reason. For regret is an expression for the occurrence of a will in the future directed toward abandoning some act in the future, and the occurrence of wills and aversions in the heart is not by the servant's act, because the servant's act is preceded by a will. So if wills were the servant's act, the servant would need another will to produce that will, and this would lead to an infinite regress, which is impossible. So we know that the occurrence of wills and aversions in the heart is only by Allah's creating and originating them. Since repentance is an expression for regret and resolve, and all of that is of the kind of wills and aversions, we know that repentance does not occur for the servant except by Allah's creation. Thus this proof agrees with what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates, namely His saying: ﴿or He turns to them in mercy﴾.

As for the Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites), they explained His saying ﴿or He turns to them in mercy﴾ either as Allah performing acts of grace (al-alutf), or as accepting repentance.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾, there are questions concerning it.

**First question:** If the purpose of the verse is to prohibit him from invoking curses upon the disbelievers, the statement is sound, since He called them wrongdoers because associating partners with Allah is wrongdoing. He said: ﴿Indeed, association with Allah is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman 31:13]. If its purpose is to prohibit him from invoking curses upon the Muslims who disobeyed his command, the statement is also sound, because whoever disobeys Allah has wronged himself.

**Second question:** The punishment mentioned in this verse may be intended to be the punishment of this world, namely killing and captivity, and it may be the punishment of the Hereafter. In either case, knowledge of that is entrusted to Allah.

**Third question:** His saying ﴿for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ is an independent clause, but the purpose of mentioning it is to explain the rightness of punishing them. The meaning is: or He punishes them, for if He punishes them, He punishes them only because they are wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 129:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

In this there are two issues:

The first issue: The purpose of this is to affirm what He mentioned earlier, in His saying: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾. The meaning is that command belongs only to the one who possesses dominion, and the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to none but Allah exalted. So command in the heavens and the earth belongs to none but Allah, and this is a decisive proof.

The second issue: He said ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ and did not say "who" (man), because the intended meaning is to refer to realities and essences (al-haqa'iq wal-mahiyyat), so everything is included.

As for His saying ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾: know that our companions (the Ash'aris) argue from this verse that He, glorified is He, has the right, by virtue of His divinity, to admit into Paradise all the disbelievers and rebellious, and has the right to admit into the Fire, by virtue of His divinity, all the near ones (al-muqarrabin) and the truthful (al-siddiqin), and that there is no objection against Him in doing these things. The indication of the verse upon this meaning is evident, and the rational proof also confirms it. That is because the act of the servant depends on volition (irada), and that volition is created by Allah exalted. So when Allah creates that volition he obeys, and when He creates the other kind of volition he disobeys. Thus the obedience of the servant is from Allah and his disobedience is also from Allah. The act of Allah does not make anything obligatory upon Allah whatsoever. So obedience does not necessitate reward, nor does disobedience necessitate punishment; rather everything is from Allah by virtue of His divinity, His dominance and His power. Thus what we claimed is sound: that if He willed to punish all the near ones, it would be good (hasuna) from Him, and if He willed to show mercy to all the Pharaohs, it would be good from Him as well. This proof is what the apparent meaning of His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾.

If it is said: Is it not established that He does not forgive the disbelievers, and does not punish the angels and the prophets?

We say: The implication of the verse is that if He willed He would do it, and there is no objection against Him. This degree does not require that He does or does not do it. This speech is most evident.

Then He concluded the speech with His saying: ﴿and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. The purpose is to make clear that although all of that would be good from Him, the side of mercy and forgiveness predominates, not as a matter of obligation but by way of grace and benevolence.

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 130–132:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبا أضْعافًا مُضاعَفَةً واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ ﴿واتَّقُوا النّارَ الَّتِي أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ ﴿وأطِيعُوا اللَّهَ والرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and redoubled, and fear God that you may prosper.﴾ ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿And obey God and the Messenger that you may receive mercy.﴾

اعْلَمْ أنَّ مِنَ النّاسِ مَن قالَ: إنَّهُ تَعالى لَمّا شَرَحَ عَظِيمَ نِعَمِهِ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ فِيما يَتَعَلَّقُ بِإرْشادِهِمْ إلى الأصْلَحِ لَهم في أمْرِ الدِّينِ وفي أمْرِ الجِهادِ، أتْبَعَ ذَلِكَ بِما يَدْخُلُ في الأمْرِ والنَّهْيِ والتَّرْغِيبِ والتَّحْذِيرِ فَقالَ: ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبا﴾ وعَلى هَذا التَّقْدِيرِ تَكُونُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ابْتِداءَ كَلامٍ، ولا تَعَلُّقَ لَها بِما قَبْلَها، وقالَ القَفّالُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: يُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ مُتَّصِلًا بِما تَقَدَّمَ مِن جِهَةِ أنَّ المُشْرِكِينَ إنَّما أنْفَقُوا عَلى تِلْكَ العَساكِرِ أمْوالًا جَمَعُوها بِسَبَبِ الرِّبا، فَلَعَلَّ ذَلِكَ يَصِيرُ داعِيًا لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ إلى الإقْدامِ عَلى الرِّبا حَتّى يَجْمَعُوا المالَ ويُنْفِقُوهُ عَلى العَسْكَرِ فَيَتَمَكَّنُونَ مِنَ الِانْتِقامِ مِنهم، فَلا جَرَمَ نَهاهُمُ اللَّهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ.

In His saying, ﴿doubled and redoubled﴾, there are two issues:

The first issue: In the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), a man who was owed one hundred dirhams by someone until a due date, and when the due date arrived the debtor did not have that money, would say: "Increase the amount so that I may extend the term for you." Perhaps he would make it two hundred. Then, when the second term came due, he would do the same, and so on for many terms, so that by means of those hundred he would take many times their amount. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿doubled and redoubled﴾.

The second issue: ﴿أضْعافًا﴾ (manifold) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl).

* * *

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir recited (sara'u) without a waw (i.e., *sari'u* without the conjunction), and it is so in the codices of the people of Madina and Syria. The rest recited it with the waw, and it is so in the codices of Makka and Iraq and the Codex of 'Uthman. Whoever recites with the waw treats it as conjoined to what precedes it, so the implied meaning is: *Obey Allah and the Messenger, and hasten.* Whoever omits the waw does so because he treats his saying "hasten" and His saying ﴿Say: Obey Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 32] as one thing, and because each of them is close in meaning to the other, he dropped the conjunction.

**The second issue:** It is reported from al-Kisa'i that he applied *imala* (vowel inclination) to (sari'u), to ﴿those hasten﴾ and to (nusari'u), and this is permissible because of the kasra-d *ra'* (the *ra'* carrying a kasra). Just as a fatha-d *ra'* prevents *imala*, so a kasra-d *ra'* permits inclining the vowel.

**The third issue:** They said: there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is: *And hasten to what brings about forgiveness from your Lord.* There is no doubt that what brings about forgiveness is nothing but doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden. So this is a command to hasten to doing the commanded acts and abstaining from the forbidden acts. Many of the scholars of legal theory (*usuliyyun*) have relied on this verse to argue that the apparent form of a command requires immediacy (*al-fawr*) and prohibits delay (*al-tarakhi*), and its basis is clear. The commentators have various statements on it:

*First*, Ibn 'Abbas said: it is Islam. I say: its basis is clear, because He mentioned forgiveness in an indefinite form, and what is intended is a great forgiveness, the most supreme in greatness, and that is the forgiveness achieved through Islam.

*Second*: It is reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: it is the performance of the obligatory duties (*fara'id*). Its basis is that the wording is unrestricted, so it must include the whole.

*Third*: That it is sincerity (*ikhlas*), which is the statement of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him. Its basis is that the aim of all acts of worship is sincerity, as He said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyina: 5].

*Fourth*: Abu al-'Aliya said: it is emigration (*hijra*).

*Fifth*: That it is jihad, which is the statement of al-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Ishaq. He said: because from His saying ﴿And when you set out from your family in the morning﴾ [Al 'Imran: 121] up to the completion of sixty verses, it was revealed on the day of Uhud, so all these commands and prohibitions are specific to what relates to the category of jihad.

*Sixth*: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the first takbir (*takbirat al-ihram*, the opening takbir of prayer).

*Seventh*: 'Uthman said: it is the five daily prayers.

*Eighth*: 'Ikrima said: it is all acts of obedience, because the wording is general, so it encompasses the whole.

*Ninth*: al-Asamm said: *sari'u*, that is, *hasten* to repentance from usury and sins. The basis of this is that He, exalted is He, first forbade usury, then said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾. So this indicates that what is meant by it is hastening to abandon what was previously forbidden. But what preceded is more appropriate, namely that it must be taken to mean the performance of obligatory duties and repentance from all prohibited things, because the wording is general, so there is no basis for restricting it. Then He, exalted is He, made clear that just as hastening to forgiveness is obligatory, so too hastening to Paradise is obligatory. He separated the two because forgiveness means the removal of punishment, while Paradise means the bestowal of reward. So He combined them to signal that the responsible person must attain both matters. As for describing Paradise as having a width equal to the heavens and the earth, it is known that this is not literal, because the heavens themselves cannot be a width for Paradise. So what is meant is like the width of the heavens and the earth. And here there are questions.

**The first question:** What is the meaning of its width being like the width of the heavens and the earth? There are several answers:

*The first*: What is meant is that if the heavens and the earths were made into layers, layer upon layer, such that each of those layers is a surface composed of parts that cannot be divided, and then some were joined to others as a single layer, that would be like the width of Paradise. This is an extreme of vastness that none knows but Allah.

*The second*: The Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth is only for one man, because a person only desires what becomes his possession, so the Paradise owned by each individual must be of this measure.

*The third*: Abu Muslim said: there is another aspect to this, namely that if Paradise were offered in exchange for the heavens and the earth as a sale, they would be its price. You say, when you sell one thing for another: "I offered it to him (*'aradtuhu 'alayhi*) and exchanged it for it (*'arada'tuhu bihi*)." So the term "width" (*'ard*) comes to be used in the place of equality between two things in quantity. Likewise the meaning of "value" (*qima*), because it is derived from weighing one thing against another, so that each of them is equal to the other.

*The fourth*: The purpose is to emphasize the vastness of Paradise, because there is nothing with us broader than them. A parallel is His saying: ﴿abiding therein for as long as the heavens and earth endure﴾ [Hud: 107], for the longest-lasting things with us are the heavens and the earth. So we were addressed according to what we know, and so it is here.

**The second question:** Why was width specifically mentioned?

The answer has two aspects:

*The first*: Since width is that, it is apparent that length is greater. A parallel is His saying: ﴿its linings of brocade﴾ [al-Rahman: 54]. He mentioned the linings only because it is known that they are of lesser status than the outer surface. If the lining is like this, how about the outer surface? So here too, if the width is like this, how about the length?

*The second*: al-Qaffal said: the intended meaning of "width" here is not the opposite of length; rather it is an expression for breadth, as the Arabs say: "lands that are wide" (*bilad 'arida*), and it is said: "a wide claim" (*da'wa 'arida*), meaning broad and great. The basis of this is that what has a wide width is not constricted, and what has a narrow width is thin, so width has been made a metaphor for breadth.

**The third question:** You say that Paradise is in the heaven, so how can its width be like the width of the heaven?

The answer is from two aspects:

*The first*: What we mean by saying that it is above the heavens and beneath the Throne is that. He, peace be upon him, said concerning the description of al-Firdaws: "Its ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful." And it is related that "the envoy of Heraclius asked the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'You call to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous; then where is the Fire?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Glory be to Allah! Then where is the night when the day comes?'"

The meaning, and Allah knows best, is that when the sphere turns, day occurs in one side of the world while night occurs on the opposite side. Likewise, Paradise is in the direction of height and the Fire is in the direction of the bottom. Anas ibn Malik was asked about Paradise: "Is it in the earth or in the heaven?" He said: "What earth and heaven could contain Paradise?" It was asked: "Then where is it?" He said: "Above the seven heavens, beneath the Throne."

*The second aspect*: Those who say that Paradise and the Fire are not created now, but that Allah creates them after the Resurrection has taken place, for them it is not far-fetched that Paradise is created in the place of the heavens and the Fire in the place of the earth. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿prepared for the righteous﴾, its apparent meaning indicates that Paradise and the Fire are created now, and this has already been established.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 134:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain their anger, and who pardon people; and Allah loves the good-doers﴾

Know that when Exalted is He explained that Paradise is prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), He mentioned the attributes of the God-fearing so that a person may be able to acquire Paradise through acquiring those attributes.

The first attribute is His saying: ﴿those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾, and in it there are several aspects:

The first: the meaning is that in a state of prosperity and ease, and in a state of capacity and hardship, they do not abandon spending. In sum, al-sarra' (ease) is wealth, and al-darra' (hardship) is poverty. It is related from some of the early generations (al-salaf) that he would sometimes give charity with an onion, and from ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she gave charity with a single grape.

The second: the meaning is that whether they are in joy or in grief, in hardship or in ease, they do not cease doing good to people.

The third: the meaning is that whether that good and spending pleases them, by being in accordance with their nature, or displeases them, by being against their nature, they do not abandon it. Allah began with mention of spending because it is a demanding act of obedience, and because at that time it was the most noble of acts of obedience due to the need for it in striving against the enemy and in aiding the poor among the Muslims.

The second attribute: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and who restrain their anger﴾, and in it there are two issues:

The first issue: it is said: "He restrained his anger" when he kept silent about it and did not show it, neither by word nor by deed. Al-Mubarrad said: its interpretation is that he suppressed it while being filled with it. It is said: "I stoppered the waterskin" when you filled it and sealed it. It is said: "So-and-so does not hold back on his jar" when he cannot bear anything. Every thing you seal from a watercourse, a door, or a path is a kazm (stopper), and that with which it is sealed is called al-kizama and al-sidada. A subterranean channel that flows in the belly of the earth is called kizama, because it is full of water, like the full stoppered water-skins. It is said: "So-and-so seized the kazm of so-and-so" when he seized the passage of his breath, because it is the place of being filled with breath. And "the camel kazama (held)" when it held on to what is in its belly and did not chew the cud. The meaning of His saying: ﴿and who restrain their anger﴾ is those who withhold their anger from executing it, and keep their anger inside their bodies. This attribute is one of the kinds of patience and forbearance, and it is like His saying: ﴿and when they are angry, they forgive﴾ [al-Shura: 37].

The second issue: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to carry it out, Allah fills his heart with security and faith." And he, peace be upon him, said to his companions: "Give charity!" So they gave charity of gold, silver and food. A man came to him with date peelings and gave them in charity. Another came and said: "By Allah, I have nothing with which to give charity, but I will give charity of my honour, so I will not punish anyone for what he says about me." So a delegation from that man's people came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he, peace be upon him, said: "A man among you has given charity, and Allah has accepted it from him: he gave charity of his honour." And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to carry it out, Allah will marry him to the wide-eyed houris wherever he wishes." And he, peace be upon him, said: "There are no two draughts more beloved to Allah than a draught of pain that its owner swallows with patience and good consolation, and a draught of anger that he restrains." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The strong man is not the one who is good at wrestling, but the one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Third attribute: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and who pardon people﴾. Al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is possible that this refers to what was condemned of the polytheists' practice of consuming usury, so the believers were forbidden from that and were urged to pardon the insolvent. Exalted is He said after the story of usury and debts: ﴿And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until ease; but if you give charity, it is better for you﴾ [al-Baqara: 280]. It is also possible that it is as He said regarding blood-money: ﴿but if anything is pardoned to him by his brother﴾ [al-Baqara: 178], up to His saying: ﴿and if you give charity, it is better for you﴾ [al-Baqara: 280]. It is also possible that this was because of "the anger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they mutilated Hamza and he said: 'I will surely mutilate them'", so he was urged to restrain this anger, to be patient with it, and to refrain from doing what he had said he would do of mutilation; so his leaving that act was a pardon. Exalted is He said in this story: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of what you were punished with; but if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [al-Nahl: 126]. The Prophet ﷺ said: "A servant does not become one of virtue until he joins the one who severed ties with him, pardons the one who wronged him, and gives to the one who deprived him." It is related from ʿIsa ibn Maryam, may the blessings of Allah be upon him: "Goodness is not that you do good to one who has done good to you; that is repayment. Goodness is that you do good to one who has done evil to you."

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾, know that the lam (al-lam) may be for the genus, so that it encompasses every good-doer and these mentioned are included under it; and it may be for the specific reference (al-ʿahd), so that it points to these people.

Know that doing good to others is either by bringing benefit to them or by repelling harm from them. As for bringing benefit to them, it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾, and it includes spending knowledge, by occupying oneself with teaching the ignorant and guiding the misguided, and it includes spending wealth in the ways of good and acts of worship. As for repelling harm from others, it is either in this world, which is not to occupy oneself with responding to that offence with another offence, and this is what is meant by restraining anger; or in the Hereafter, which is to clear one's account of liabilities and claims in the Hereafter, and this is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and who pardon people﴾. Thus this verse, in this respect, indicates all aspects of doing good to others. And since these three matters share the quality of being good to others, He mentioned their reward, saying: ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾, for Allah's love for the servant is the most comprehensive of the degrees of reward.

[Page 9 begins at the marked point]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who, when they commit an act of immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist in what they have done while they know.﴾ ﴿Those — their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally; and excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

Know that the coherence (nazm) of the verses is in two respects:

The first: When the Exalted described Paradise as prepared for the God-fearing (muttaqun), He explained that the God-fearing are of two categories:

One of them: those who turned to acts of obedience and worship, and they are the ones whom Allah described as spending in ease and hardship, restraining anger, and pardoning people.

The second: those who committed sins and then repented, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿And those who, when they commit an act of immorality﴾.

[Page 10 begins at the marked point]

He (the Exalted) explained that this group is like the first group in being God-fearing, because the sinner who repents from his sin becomes, in his standing for rank and honour before Allah, like one who never sinned at all.

The second respect: In the first verse He urged kindness to others, and in this verse He urged kindness to oneself, for the sinner who disobeyed and then repents, that repentance is a kindness from him to his own self. And in the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn ʿAbbas narrated that this verse was revealed concerning two men, one from the Ansar and one from Thaqif, whom the Messenger (ﷺ) had made brothers, and they were never apart in their affairs. The Thaqafi went out with the Messenger (ﷺ) on a journey by lot, and he left the Ansari behind to look after his family. The Ansari used to do so, then he went to his wife to kiss her, but she placed her palm over her face. The man regretted this, and when the Thaqafi returned with the Messenger (ﷺ) he did not see the Ansari, who had wandered off into the mountains in repentance. When the Messenger (ﷺ) learned of this he remained silent until this verse was revealed. And Ibn Masʿud said: The believers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Children of Israel were more honoured by Allah than us. If one of them committed a sin, the expiation of his sin would be written on the threshold of his house: 'Slit your nose, do such-and-such.'" So Allah revealed this verse and explained that they (the Muslims) are more honoured by Allah than them, since He made the expiation of their sins to be seeking forgiveness.

The second issue: The word "immorality" (fāḥishah) here is an omitted adjective, and the estimated phrase is: "they committed an act that is immoral." Scholars mentioned several differences between "immorality" and "wronging oneself":

The first: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: "Immorality" is that whose commission is complete in ugliness, while wronging oneself is any sin for which a person is held accountable.

The second: "Immorality" is the major sin, and wronging oneself is the minor sin, and minor sins also require seeking forgiveness, as evidenced by the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek forgiveness, in His words: ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Muhammad: 19], and his seeking forgiveness did not indicate minor sins but rather the leaving of what is better.

The third: "Immorality" is fornication, and wronging oneself is the kiss, the touch, and the glance. This is according to those who interpreted the verse in light of the cause (sabab) we have narrated. Also, because the Exalted called fornication "immorality," He said: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an immorality﴾ [al-Isra: 32].

As for His words ﴿they remembered Allah﴾, there are two views:

One: The meaning is that they remembered Allah's threat, or His punishment, or His majesty which necessitates fear and shame before Him. This would be an instance of omitting a modifier (ḥadhf al-muḍāf), and "remembrance" here is the opposite of forgetfulness. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Ḍaḥḥak, Muqatil, and al-Waqidi. For al-Ḍaḥḥak said: "They remembered the Great Gathering before Allah," and Muqatil and al-Waqidi said: "They reflected that Allah would question them." This is because He said after this verse: ﴿so they sought forgiveness for their sins﴾, which indicates that seeking forgiveness is like an effect and result of that remembrance. It is known that the remembrance that necessitates seeking forgiveness is nothing but remembrance of Allah's punishment, His prohibition, and His threat. A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, remember (Allah), and at once they see clearly﴾ [al-Araf: 201].

The second view: The intended remembrance here is remembrance of Allah through praise, glorification, and exaltation. This is because whoever wishes to ask Allah for something should precede that request with praise of Allah. Here, since the intended matter was seeking forgiveness for sins, they preceded it with praise of Allah the Exalted, and then they occupied themselves with seeking forgiveness from their sins.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿so they sought forgiveness for their sins﴾, and what is meant by it is bringing repentance in its correct form, which is regret for what has passed together with resolve not to repeat its like in the future. This is the true reality of repentance. As for seeking forgiveness with the tongue alone, it has no effect in removing the sin. Rather, it is necessary to make this seeking of forgiveness apparent, both to remove suspicion and to show that one has devoted oneself to Allah the Exalted. His words "for their sins" mean "on account of their sins."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ The purpose of this is that the servant should not seek forgiveness except from Him, because He, the Exalted, is the one able to punish the servant in this world and the Hereafter, so He is the one able to remove that punishment from him. Thus it is established that seeking forgiveness is not permissible except from Him.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and do not persist in what they have done﴾. Know that His words ﴿and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ are a parenthetical sentence between the conjoined and the conjoined-to. The estimated meaning is: "they sought forgiveness for their sins and did not persist in what they had done."

His words ﴿while they know﴾ have two views:

The first: It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the act of persisting. The estimated meaning is: "and they did not persist in what they had done of sins while they were aware that they were forbidden and prohibited," because one who does not know that an act is prohibited may be excused, whereas one who knows its prohibition is in no way excused for his act.

The second: The intended meaning is reason, discernment, and the capacity to refrain from immoralities. This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The pen is lifted from three."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Those — their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. The meaning is that two things are sought:

The first: Security from punishment, and this is indicated by His words: ﴿forgiveness from their Lord﴾.

The second: Delivering reward to them, which is what is meant by His words: ﴿and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally﴾. Then the Exalted explained that what they obtain of that, namely forgiveness and the gardens, is a wage for their deeds and a recompense for them, by His words: ﴿and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: "This refutes the view of those who say that reward is a bounty from Allah and not a recompense for their deeds."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verse 137:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly there have passed before you examples; so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied.﴾ ﴿This is a clarification for mankind, and guidance and an admonition for the righteous.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, promised forgiveness and gardens in return for obedience and repentance from disobedience, He followed this with mention of what moves them to perform obedience and to repent from disobedience, namely contemplating the conditions of the earlier generations, the obedient and the disobedient. So He said: ﴿Certainly there have passed before you examples﴾. There are several issues concerning this verse:

The first issue: al-Wahidi said: The root of khuluww (passing away) in the language is solitude; an empty place is one isolated from whoever dwells in it. It is also used for time, in the sense of having passed, because what has passed has been separated from existence and has become empty of it. Likewise the past nations (al-umam al-khaliyah). As for sunnah (way, custom), it is the straight path and the followed example. There are several opinions on the derivation of this word:

The first: it is a form (fu'lah) from sanna al-ma' yasunnuhu, when one pours water continuously; sann means pouring water. The Arabs likened the straight path to poured water, for the successive parts of water flowing in one course become like a single thing. Thus sunnah is a form (fu'lah) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul).

The second: that it is from sanantu al-nasl wa al-sinan asunnuhu sannan, fa-huwa masnun, when you sharpen it on the whetstone (misann). So the act attributed to the Prophet ﷺ was called sunnah in the sense that it has been sharpened (masnun).

The third: that it is from the saying of them: sanna al-ibil, when he pastured the camels well. The act which the Prophet ﷺ persistently observed was called sunnah in the sense that he, peace be upon him, took excellent care of it and maintained it.

The second issue: The meaning of the verse: there have passed before you the sunan of Allah, exalted is He, concerning the earlier nations. The scholars differed on this. Most of the exegetes hold that the intended meaning is the sunan of destruction and annihilation, based on the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿so observe how was the end of those who denied﴾. That is because they opposed the prophets and messengers out of greed for this world and pursuit of its pleasures; then they perished, and no trace of their worldly life remained, while the curse in this world and punishment in the Hereafter remained upon them. So Allah, exalted is He, encouraged the community of Muhammad ﷺ to contemplate the conditions of those who passed, so that this would move them to faith in Allah and His messengers, and to turn away from leadership in this world and the pursuit of status. Mujahid said: Rather, the intended meaning is the sunan of Allah, exalted is He, concerning the disbelievers and the believers; for the world does not remain with the believer nor with the disbeliever, but the believer is left after his death with a good reputation in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is left with the curse in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿so observe how was the end of those who denied﴾, because contemplating the condition of one of the two groups suffices for knowing the condition of the other. Also it is said that the purpose of it is to deter the disbelievers from their disbelief, and this is known only by contemplating the conditions of the deniers and the obstinate. A parallel to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly Our word had preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be helped, and that Our host would indeed be the victors﴾ [al-Saffat: 171-173], and His saying: ﴿and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-A'raf: 128], and His saying: ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105].

The third issue: His saying ﴿so travel through the earth and observe﴾ [al-Nahl: 36] does not necessarily mean a command to do so; rather the aim is to know their conditions. If this knowledge is obtained without travelling through the earth, the purpose is achieved. It is also not impossible to say that witnessing the traces of those who came before has a stronger effect than hearing about them, as the poet said:

Indeed our traces point to us, so observe after us the traces.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿This is a clarification for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing.﴾ By His saying "This" He means what has preceded of His commands, His prohibitions, His promises and His threats, and His mention of various kinds of clear proofs and signs. It is necessary to distinguish between bayan (clarification), huda (guidance) and mawizah (admonition), since conjunction (al-'atf) requires difference. So we say that there are two aspects to this:

The first: bayan is the indication that removes doubt after the doubt has arisen. The distinction is that bayan is general, in whatever sense it occurs, whereas huda is the clarification of the path of right guidance so that it may be followed rather than the path of error. As for mawizah, it is speech that provides restraint from what is not fitting in the path of religion. The upshot is that bayan is a genus under which there are two kinds:

One of them: speech that guides to what is fitting in religion, and this is huda.

The second: speech that restrains from what is not fitting in religion, and this is mawizah.

The second aspect: bayan is indication, whereas huda is indication on condition that it leads to being guided. This discussion has already been covered in the explanation of His saying: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ in Surat al-Baqarah.

The fourth issue: concerning the restriction of this clarification, guidance and admonition to the God-fearing, there are two aspects:

One of them: they are the ones who benefit from it, so these things are, with respect to those other than the God-fearing, as though they did not exist. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45], ﴿You can only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir: 28]. Its establishment has already been explained in the explanation of His saying: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2].

The second: His saying ﴿This is a clarification for mankind﴾ is a general statement, and then His saying ﴿and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ is specific, except with respect to the God-fearing. And Allah knows best what is correct.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will be the superior ones, if you are believers.﴾

Know that what He mentioned before, His words ﴿Similar ways have passed before you﴾ and His words ﴿This is a clarification for mankind﴾, serves as an introduction to His words ﴿Do not weaken, nor grieve.﴾ It is as if He said: when you investigate the conditions of the earlier generations, you will know that the people of falsehood, even if they enjoy a momentary assault, the outcome of their affair is decline and weakening, while the state of the people of truth becomes exalted and the assault of the people of falsehood fades away. Therefore, the assault of the disbelievers against you on the day of Uhud should not become a cause of weakness in your hearts, of your cowardice, or of your incapacity. Rather, your hearts must be strengthened, for superiority will surely be attained by you, and power and dominion will return to you.

Then we say: His words ﴿Do not weaken﴾ mean: do not become weak in jihad (striving in the cause of Allah). Al-wahn is weakness. The Exalted said, relating the words of Zakariyya, upon him be peace: ﴿Indeed, my bones have weakened﴾ [Maryam: 4]. His words ﴿nor grieve﴾ mean: over those among you who were killed or wounded. His words ﴿and you will be the superior ones﴾ have several interpretations:

The first: your condition is superior to theirs in terms of killing, because on the day of Badr you inflicted on them more than they inflicted on you on the day of Uhud. This is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿What! When a disaster struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "From where is this?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 165]. Or, because your fighting is for Allah and their fighting is for Satan. Or, because their fighting is for a false religion and your fighting is for the true religion. All of these necessitate that your condition is superior to theirs.

The second: the meaning is that you will be the superior ones through proof, adherence to the religion, and the praiseworthy end.

The third: the meaning is that you will be the superior ones in that, in the end, you will triumph over them and gain mastery over them. This is very well suited to what precedes it, because their hearts were broken on account of that weakness, so they needed something that would grant them strength in the heart and joy in the soul. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, gave them this glad tidings. As for His words ﴿if you are believers﴾, there are several interpretations:

The first: "and you will be the superior ones if you remain upon your faith." The purpose is to show that Allah, the Exalted, undertook to elevate their rank only for the sake of their adherence to the religion of Islam.

The second: "and you will be the superior ones, so be affirmers of this glad tiding, if you are affirmers of what Allah promises you and gives you good news of, namely victory."

The third: the sense is: "Do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will be the superior ones, if you are believers." For Allah, the Exalted, has promised the support of this religion. So if you are among the believers, you will know that this present calamity will not remain in its state, that the dominion will pass to the Muslims, and that gaining mastery over the enemy will be attained by them.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 3, verses 140–141 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has already touched the people. We alternate these days among the people, so that Allah may know those who believe, and take martyrs from among you. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.﴾

Know that this is part of His saying: ﴿Do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be the superior ones﴾. Allah the Exalted thus explains that the wound that afflicts them does not necessarily remove their determination and their striving in fighting the enemy. This is because, just as that befell them, a similar wound had already befallen their enemy before that. So if they, despite their falsehood and the evil of their end, did not slacken in war because of it, then it is more fitting that weakness should not overtake you, given the goodness of the outcome and your adherence to the truth. There are several issues in the verse:

The first issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr, from ʿAsim, read (qarḥ) with a ḍammah on the qaf, and likewise His saying: (after the wound had befallen them) [Al ʿImran: 172]. The rest read it with a fatḥah on the qaf in both places. They differed in several respects:
The first: both have the same meaning; they are two dialects, like al-juhd and al-jahd, al-wujd and al-wajd, al-ḍuʿf and al-ḍaʿf.
The second: the fatḥah is the dialect of Tihamah and the Hijaz, and the ḍammah is the dialect of Najd.
The third: with the fatḥah it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and with the ḍammah it is a noun (ism).
The fourth, which is the view of al-Farra': with the fatḥah it is the wound itself, and with the ḍammah it is the pain of the wound.
The fifth: Ibn Miqsam said: they are two dialects, except that the fatḥah form gives the impression that it is the plural of qarḥah.

The second issue: there are two opinions regarding the verse:
One of them: "If a wound touches you" means a wound on the day of Uhud; "then it has already touched them" means on the day of Badr. This is like His saying: ﴿Why, when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, did you say, "How is this?"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 165].
The second: the disbelievers had also suffered on the day of Uhud a similar amount of wounds and killing as you did, for more than twenty of their men were killed, the bearer of their standard was killed, their wounds were many, and most of their horses were hamstrung with arrows. Moreover, the defeat had come upon them at the beginning of the day.

If it is said: how can He say "a similar wound" when their wound on the day of Uhud was not like the wound of the polytheists?
We say: on this interpretation, the wound must be understood as mere defeat, not as the great number of the slain.

* * *

Then He the Exalted says: ﴿and We alternate these days among the people﴾, and there are issues in this:

The first issue: (tilka) is the subject, (al-ayyam) is its attribute, and (nudawiluha) is its predicate. It is also permissible to say that "tilka al-ayyam" is a subject and predicate, as you say: "They are the days that wear out every new thing." So His saying "and those days" refers to all the days of the wondrous events, and He explains that they are turns that come upon a man for a time and then for another time, and war is a matter of alternation (sijal).

The second issue: al-Qaffal said: al-mudawalah is the transfer of a thing from one to another. It is said: "the hands passed it around" (tadawalat-hu al-aydi) when they handed it from one to another. From this is His saying: ﴿so that it does not become a circulating commodity among the rich among you﴾ [al-Hashr: 7], i.e., you pass it around among yourselves and do not give the poor a share of it. It is also said: "the world is turns" (dwal), i.e., it moves from one people to another, and then from them to others. It is also said: "the time turned (dala) for him with such-and-such" when it moved to him. The meaning is that the days of this world are turns among people; neither their pleasures nor their pains endure, so one day there comes joy to one and grief to his enemy, and another day is the reverse. Nothing of its conditions remains and no trace of its effects is fixed.

Know that this alternation does not mean that Allah the Exalted sometimes helps the believers and at other times helps the disbelievers; this is because the help of Allah is a noble station and a great honour, which does not befit the disbeliever. Rather, the meaning of this alternation is that He sometimes intensifies the trial upon the disbelievers and at other times upon the believers, and the benefit in this is of several kinds:

The first: if He intensified the trial upon the disbelievers at all times and removed it from the believers at all times, there would arise a necessary knowledge that faith is true and whatever else is false,
[Page 14]
and if that were so, obligation, reward and punishment would be voided. For this reason Allah sometimes sends the trial upon the people of faith, and at other times upon the people of disbelief, so that doubts remain and the responsible person repels them by reflecting on the proofs that indicate the soundness of Islam, and thus his reward with Allah becomes greater.

The second: the believer may commit some sins, so the intensification of the trial upon him in this world is a form of discipline from Allah for him. As for the intensification of the trial upon the disbeliever, it is a wrath from Allah upon him.

The third: the pleasures and pains of this world do not endure, and its conditions are not constant; lasting happiness is attained only in the abode of the Hereafter. For this reason He causes death after life and sickness after health. If that is good, why would it not be good for Him to exchange ease for hardship and power for weakness? It is narrated that Abu Sufyan climbed the mountain on the day of Uhud and then said: "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" Then ʿUmar said: "This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, ʿUmar." Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day, and the days are turns, and war is a matter of alternation." ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There is no equality. Our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in Hellfire." He said: "If it is as you claim, then we have indeed lost and suffered loss."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and so that Allah may know those who believe﴾, there are issues in this.

The first issue: the lam in His saying ﴿and so that Allah may know﴾ is connected to a hidden verb, either after it or before it. As for the hidden verb after it, the sense is: ﴿and so that Allah may know those who believe﴾ We made this alternation. As for the hidden verb before it, the sense is: "And those days We alternate among the people for several reasons, among them so that Allah may know those who believe, among them that He may take martyrs from among you, among them that Allah may purify those who believe, among them that He may destroy the disbelievers." All of these are like the cause and reason for that alternation.

The second issue: the waw in His saying ﴿and so that Allah may know those who believe﴾ has many parallels in the Qur'an. Allah says: ﴿and so that he may be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75], and He says: ﴿and so that the hearts of those who do not believe may incline to it﴾ [al-An'am: 113]. The sense is: "And those days We alternate among the people so that such-and-such may be, and so that Allah may know." The thing coordinated with is omitted to signal that the wisdom in this alternation is not one thing, in order to console them for what happened, and to make them aware that in that event and their situation in it there are aspects of wisdom which, if they knew them, would gladden them.

The third issue: the apparent meaning of His saying ﴿and so that Allah may know those who believe﴾ indicates that He did that alternation in order to acquire this knowledge, and it is known that this is impossible for Allah the Exalted. A similar difficulty in this verse is found in His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the steadfast?﴾ [Al ʿImran: 142], and His saying: ﴿And We had certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful and will surely know the liars﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 3], and His saying: ﴿That We may know which of the two parties is more precise in computing what they remained in terms of time﴾ [al-Kahf: 12], and His saying: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast﴾, and His saying: ﴿except that We might know who follows the Messenger﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], and His saying: ﴿to test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Hud: 7]. Hisham ibn al-Hakam argued from the apparent meanings of these verses that Allah the Exalted does not know the occurrence of events except at the time they occur. He said: all these verses indicate that He became knowing of these things only when they occurred.

The Mutakallimun answered him: rational proofs have established that He the Exalted knows events before they occur, so it is established that change in knowledge is impossible. However, applying the word "knowledge" to the known and "power" to the powered is a well-known metaphor. It is said: "This is the knowledge of so-and-so," meaning what is known by him, and "This is the power of so-and-so," meaning what is within his power. So every verse whose apparent meaning suggests a renewal of knowledge, what is meant is a renewal of the known.

[Page 15]
Having understood this, we say: in this verse there are several aspects:

One of them: that the sincere be made distinct from the hypocrite, and the believer from the disbeliever.

The second: that He may know the friends of Allah, and He attributed them to Himself as an honour.

The third: that He may judge distinction; He placed "knowledge" in the place of "judgment of distinction," because judgment of distinction only takes place after knowledge.

The fourth: that He may know it as having occurred from them, just as He knew that it would occur; for reward falls upon what has happened, not upon what is known but has not come into existence.

The fourth issue: knowledge may be such that it requires only one object, as one says: "I know Zayd," meaning I know his essence and recognise him. It may also require two objects, as one says: "I know Zayd generous." The meaning here is this second kind, except that the second object is omitted. The sense is: "And so that Allah may know those who believe as distinguished by faith from others," i.e., the wisdom in this alternation is that those who believe become distinguished from those who claim faith, by means of their patience and their steadfastness in Islam. It is also possible that knowledge here is of the first kind, meaning acquaintance with the essence, and the sense is: "and so that Allah may know those who believe, by what appears of their patience in striving against their enemy," i.e., that He may recognise them by their very persons; but the cause of the occurrence of this knowledge, which is the manifestation of patience, is omitted here.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and take martyrs from among you﴾, what is meant is mention of the second wisdom in that alternation, and there are issues in it:

The first issue: there are two opinions regarding this verse:
The first: "takes martyrs from among you" means witnesses over people for what has proceeded from them of sins and disobediences, for their being witnesses over people is a lofty station and an exalted rank.
The second: what is meant is "and that He may honour a people with martyrdom." This is because a group of Muslims had missed the day of Badr and used to wish to meet the enemy and that there might be for them a day like the day of Badr in which they would fight the enemy and seek martyrdom. Also, the Qur'an is filled with the exaltation of the state of martyrs. Allah says: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al ʿImran: 169]; He says: ﴿And the prophets and the martyrs will be brought forward﴾ [al-Zumar: 69]; and He says: ﴿Those will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. Thus this station is the third station after prophethood, and if that is so, then among the desired benefits of that alternation is the attainment of this great rank by some of the believers.

The second issue: our companions (the Ash'arites) argued from this verse that all events occur by the will of Allah the Exalted. They said: the station of martyrdom is as you have mentioned; if it were possible to attain it without the disbelievers being empowered over the believers, there would be no sense in the causal explanation; and if it is not possible, then the killing of the believers by the disbelievers is a necessary consequence of that martyrdom. So if attaining that martyrdom for the servant is willed by Allah the Exalted, then that killing must also be willed by Allah the Exalted. Moreover, His saying ﴿and take martyrs from among you﴾ explicitly states that that by which that martyrdom was obtained is from Allah the Exalted, and this indicates that the act of the servant is the creation of Allah the Exalted.

The third issue: "shuhada'" is the plural of "shahid," like "kuramaʾ" and "ẓurafaʾ." The Muslim killed by the sword of the disbelievers is a shahid. Regarding the explanation of this name there are several views:
The first: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: the martyrs are alive, based on His saying: ﴿but they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al ʿImran: 169]. So their spirits are living and have attended the Abode of Peace, whereas the spirits of others do not witness it.
The second: [Page 16 continues]

Ibn al-Anbari: Because God Most High and His angels testified to him (the martyr) of Paradise, so "shahid" is a fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (mafa'il, one who is witnessed to).

The third view: They were called "shuhada'" (witnesses) because on the Day of Resurrection they will bear witness together with the prophets and the truthful (siddiqin), as God Most High said: ﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143].

The fourth view: They were called "shuhada'" because just as they were killed, they were admitted into Paradise. The evidence is that the disbelievers, just as they died, were admitted into the Fire, as shown by His saying: ﴿They were drowned and then admitted into Fire﴾ [Nuh: 25]. Likewise here, it must be said: those who were killed in the way of God, just as they died, entered Paradise.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿And God does not love the wrongdoers﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: that is, the polytheists (mushrikin), due to His saying: ﴿Indeed, association [with God] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. It is an interjection (i'tiraD) between one part of the reasoning and another. There are several aspects to it:

The first: God does not love whoever is not steadfast in faith and patient in jihad.

The second: It contains an indication that God Most High only grants the disbelievers victory over the believers for the benefits He mentioned, not because He loves them.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And that God may purify those who believe﴾, that is, to cleanse them of their sins and remove them from them. Al-mahs in the language means purification (tanqiyah), and al-mahq in the language means diminution (nuqsan). Al-Mufaddal said: it is for a thing to go away entirely until nothing of it is seen. From this is His saying: ﴿God destroys interest﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276], that is, uproots it. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of the verse is that God Most High made the days alternate between the Muslims and the disbelievers. If victory goes to the disbelievers over the believers, the intended meaning is the purification of the believers' sins; and if victory goes to the believers over those disbelievers, the intended meaning is the obliteration and erasure of the disbelievers' traces. Thus He contrasted the purification of the believers with the annihilation of the disbelievers, because the purification of the former through the destruction of their sins is like the annihilation of the latter through the destruction of themselves. This is a subtle contrast in meaning. The closer view is that the intended "disbelievers" here is a specific group of them, namely those who fought the Messenger ﷺ on the day of Uhud. We say this because we know that God did not annihilate all the disbelievers, but many of them remained in their disbelief. And God knows best.
